stories.headline: 86% Voted to Open Beacon Hill’s Records. Asked if He’ll Comply, Speaker Mariano: “Get Someone Polite With Some Manners.”
stories.deck: Asked on camera whether he’ll honor Question 1 or work to overturn it, the Massachusetts House speaker said: “I’m not going to tell you my plan right now.”
stories.body:
Voters passed Question 1 with nearly 86 percent, putting the Legislature and the governor’s office under the public records law on Jan. 1.

A Mass Fiscal Alliance staffer asked House Speaker Ron Mariano: “Will you comply or will you work to overturn the election results?”

Mariano: “I’m not going to tell you my plan right now. I don’t like the rudeness of your approach.”

Then: “Get someone polite with some manners that can ask me those questions.”

Governor Healey says she’ll “absolutely” comply. Mariano argued in June the question’s enforcement setup is “clearly unconstitutional when applied to the legislative branch.”
stories.pull_quote: Get someone polite with some manners that can ask me those questions.

record.label: Mass Fiscal Alliance video, posted 5:12 p.m. ET: staffer asks “Will you comply or will you work to overturn the election results?”; Mariano: “I’m not going to tell you my plan right now. I don’t like the rudeness of your approach.”; “Why should I cooperate with it?”; “Get someone polite with some manners that can ask me those questions.”; “But until that time, I’m not talking to you.” (FNN transcript of the 2:10 video)
Same exchange; House and Senate records bills in conference committee since the end of July; Mariano in June: enforcement setup “clearly unconstitutional when applied to the legislative branch”
Healey said she would “absolutely” comply; Question 1 approved with nearly 86 percent, unofficial results
Massachusetts the only state where the governor’s office, Legislature and judiciary all claim to be completely exempt from public records requirements
Question 1 text: makes most records of the Legislature and the governor’s office public records; “This act shall take effect on January 1, 2027”

image.alt: FNN graphic: get someone polite

share.line: 86% of Massachusetts voters opened Beacon Hill’s records. Asked if he’ll comply, Speaker Ron Mariano: “Get someone polite with some manners that can ask me those questions.”
share.caption: “GET SOMEONE POLITE WITH SOME MANNERS”

stories.headline: Musk Says Duffy Turned Down Free Starlinks for the FAA. Duffy: “Our Airspace Is Very Big.” Musk: 🤦‍♂️
stories.deck: Days after the ground stop, Musk wrote “As it turns out, they were” needed. Duffy calls Starlink “remarkable” but says the FAA chose a ground network.
stories.body:
Three days after the FAA’s Nov. 13 ground stop, Elon Musk posted: “Free Starlinks for FAA were offered to Sec Duffy, but he said they were not needed. As it turns out, they were.”

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy answered Tuesday: “I think what he’s doing with Starlink and the speed is remarkable, but our airspace is very big.”

Duffy said an earlier Starlink version hit “some issues” in the FAA’s tech lab, so “we thought that the best method is to have a network that’s based on the ground.”

Musk’s reply: 🤦‍♂️

Early Wednesday: “I wrote this 18 months ago.”
stories.pull_quote: As it turns out, they were.

record.label: Musk, 4:47 p.m. ET: “As I was saying … Free Starlinks for FAA were offered to Sec Duffy, but he said they were not needed. As it turns out, they were.”

Duffy on camera (clip posted 3:39 p.m. ET): “Starlink was a great solution for some of our assets in Alaska”; “we sent Starlink in one of its prior iterations to our tech lab and there was some issues”; “we thought that the best method is to have a network that’s based on the ground”; “I think what he’s doing with Starlink and the speed is remarkable, but our airspace is very big.” (FNN transcript of the 45-second clip)
Musk, 4:55 p.m. ET, quoting the Duffy clip: 🤦‍♂️
Musk, 12:26 a.m. ET: “I wrote this 18 months ago,” quoting his Feb. 27, 2025 post
Musk, 10:09 a.m. ET: “the Verizon communication system to air traffic control is breaking down very rapidly”; “The Starlink terminals are being sent at NO COST”
Musk’s correction, 2:24 p.m. ET: “the ancient system that is rapidly declining in capability was made L3Harris. The new system that is not yet operational is from Verizon.”
Duffy explained the ground-based choice; Starlink used for some assets in Alaska; Duffy said the routers being replaced were about 25 years old
Duffy, March 2025, on Starlink: “It’s not. It’s part of the solution”

image.alt: FNN graphic: our airspace is very big

share.line: Musk: “Free Starlinks for FAA were offered to Sec Duffy, but he said they were not needed. As it turns out, they were.” Duffy: “Our airspace is very big.” Musk: 🤦‍♂️
share.caption: “AS IT TURNS OUT, THEY WERE.”

stories.headline: Tesla Unveils Powercore: Transformer, Inverter and Breaker in One Box. “Made in America. Operating 2027.”
stories.deck: Rated 7.4 MW continuously at 34.5 kV. Musk: “Advanced solid state transformers at scale from Tesla.” Transformer lead times have run as long as four years.
stories.body:
Tesla’s Megapack team introduced Powercore on Tuesday: a “Solid state medium voltage transformer, inverter and breaker” rated 7.4 MW, or 9 MVA, continuously at 34.5 kV. “Made in America. Operating 2027.”

Musk’s summary: “Advanced solid state transformers at scale from Tesla.”

The pitch: one unit does the jobs of separate inverters and a big oil-filled transformer. Electrek lists peak efficiency of 98.86% and a warranty of up to 25 years.

Conventional transformers have had lead times as long as four years, pv magazine reports.

Pricing, customers and a factory location haven’t been announced.
stories.pull_quote: Made in America. Operating 2027

record.label: Tesla Megapack, 11:00 a.m. ET: “Introducing Powercore / Solid state medium voltage transformer, inverter and breaker – reliable, safe and secure / 7.4 MW/9 MVA continuously at 34.5 kVac w/ grid-forming support for 10MVA of peak power / Made in America. Operating 2027”
Musk, 11:46 a.m. ET: “Advanced solid state transformers at scale from Tesla”

Spec sheet: peak efficiency 98.86%; warranty up to 25 years; no flammable oil; one solid-state unit replaces low-voltage inverters plus an oil-filled transformer; “Tesla still hasn’t shared pricing, customers, or a factory location”; Heron Power plans its own solid-state transformer in 2027
Transformer input shortages “caused lead times of as long as four years”; to be manufactured at Tesla facilities in the U.S.; working with NVIDIA on DSX Ready certification

image.alt: FNN graphic: Powercore

share.line: Tesla’s new Powercore: transformer, inverter and breaker in one unit, 7.4 MW at 34.5 kV. “Made in America. Operating 2027.”
share.caption: “MADE IN AMERICA. OPERATING 2027.”

stories.headline: Ex-CNN Anchor Chris Cuomo: “The Russia Probe Was Exaggerated and Overextended for Political Effect. It’s True.”
stories.deck: In 2018 he told a Republican congressman there were “clearly grounds for suspicion to look.” On his podcast Tuesday: “I wish I had seen that differently.”
stories.body:
In May 2018, CNN’s Chris Cuomo pushed back on Rep. Peter King, the New York Republican who said the Russia investigation had no basis: “it seems like there was clearly grounds for suspicion to look.”

On Tuesday’s Chris Cuomo Project: “The Russia probe was exaggerated and overextended for political effect. It’s true. I wish I had seen that differently.”

And: “that probe went on too long and in too many different directions that yielded nothing.”

His fine print: “Russian interference is real,” and Trump’s team took meetings that “created suspicion.”
stories.pull_quote: The Russia probe was exaggerated and overextended for political effect. It’s true.

record.label: Episode “This Is the Worst Thing Trump Has Ever Done,” on his official channel
record.source: The Chris Cuomo Project on YouTube

record.label: Podcast published 6:30 a.m. ET; between 23:15 and 33:58: “Russian interference is real, by the way. The Russia probe was exaggerated and overextended for political effect. It’s true. I wish I had seen that differently. There are plenty of meetings that Trump’s guys shouldn’t have taken, and they created suspicion, and it’s on them. But that probe went on too long and in too many different directions that yielded nothing.” He adds the Trump administration “somewhat legitimized those extra efforts by trying to obstruct”
21-second clip, posted 4:15 p.m. ET (FNN transcript matches the podcast transcript)

Cuomo to Rep. Peter King on CNN: “You have had so many points of contacts, so many bad choices made by people in and around that campaign about what to say and do it seems like there was clearly grounds for suspicion to look.”

stories.headline: South Africa’s President Wants Musk to “Give Back.” Musk: “South Africa Is Now Super Racist Against Whites and Asians.”
stories.deck: Ramaphosa told ABC’s Jonathan Karl he’d like to chat with Musk about “remembering his country.” Starlink still has no South African licence.
stories.body:
South African President Cyril Ramaphosa, visiting Silicon Valley, told ABC’s Jonathan Karl on Monday: “I have met Elon Musk in the past, and I’ve been awed by his brilliance. But I’d also like to chat to him about remembering his country.”

Musk, he said, should “give back to this country.”

Musk’s reply: “South Africa is now super racist against Whites and Asians.”

The backdrop, per ITWeb: licence holders must be at least 30% owned by historically disadvantaged groups. Starlink offered to connect 5,000 mostly rural schools instead. Still no licence.

Ramaphosa says Musk “doesn’t fully understand” apartheid’s harm.
stories.pull_quote: South Africa is now super racist against Whites and Asians.

record.label: Semafor, 3:10 p.m. ET: “I have met Elon Musk in the past, and I’ve been awed by his brilliance. But I’d also like to chat to him about remembering his country,” Ramaphosa tells @jonkarl; “What you’ve become today is by dint of your own origins”
Musk, 9:09 p.m. ET, replying to Semafor: “South Africa is now super racist against Whites and Asians”

Interview at Semafor’s Silicon Valley event Nov. 16; Musk should “give back to this country”; “he doesn’t fully understand the extent of what the apartheid policies did to black South Africans”; Electronic Communications Act requires individual licence-holders to have at least 30% ownership by historically disadvantaged groups; Starlink previously offered to connect 5 000 predominantly rural schools; “Starlink has yet to secure the licences”
Ramaphosa: “When the apartheid government spent R12 on his education, it spent R1 on my education”; licence rule requires at least 30% ownership by historically disadvantaged groups
Ramaphosa on Starlink: “There have been discussions and they revolve around policies. And he is one of those who has had difficulty in understanding the policy position”

stories.headline: Pressley’s To-Do List for the New Democratic Majority Starts With “Reparations.” Her Dare to Trump: Veto It.
stories.deck: The Boston Democrat posted her priorities Sunday, from reparations to abolishing ICE. Overriding a veto takes two-thirds of both chambers.
stories.body:
Rep. Ayanna Pressley of Massachusetts posted her plan for the Democratic majority that takes over Congress in January: “Reparations. Abortion justice. Medicare for All. Abolishing ICE. Childcare. Paid leave. And more.”

Her dare: “If Trump wants to veto any of this, then the people will know exactly where he stands.”

The Constitution’s fine print: an override needs two thirds of each House.

Back in her own city, Boston paid Tufts $335,000 for the first volume of its reparations study. The report was canceled, and Tufts returned the full $335,000, GBH reported.

First word on her list: Reparations.
stories.pull_quote: If Trump wants to veto any of this, then the people will know exactly where he stands.

record.label: Pressley, 6:30 p.m. ET: “We need to show people what Democrats can do with our majority. Reparations. Abortion justice. Medicare for All. Abolishing ICE. Childcare. Paid leave. And more. If Trump wants to veto any of this, then the people will know exactly where he stands. And we won’t stop fighting until we win.”
Same message posted as a Substack note
Pressley, 10:56 a.m. ET: “Under this new Democratic majority, I’ll keep pushing for reparations”; pushing to pass H.R. 40
Graphic billed as “Rep. Ayanna Pressley’s Majority Priorities”; 13 items, including H.R. 40, “Affordable Housing” and “Lower Costs”
Article I, Section 7: a returned bill becomes law only if “two thirds of that House shall agree to pass the Bill” and it is “approved by two thirds” of the other
City and Tufts “reluctantly come to a decision to cancel the contract for the first volume of the report”; “Tufts returned the full value of the contract — $335,000 — to the city”

stories.headline: Rubio to the International Criminal Court: “Americans Have Never Agreed to Submit to the ICC’s Authority”
stories.deck: In his first prepared speech since the midterms, the Secretary of State told the Federalist Society America won’t bow to “soulless global bureaucrats.”
stories.body:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio told the Federalist Society’s national convention in Washington on Friday what America thinks of the International Criminal Court.

“Americans have never agreed to submit to the ICC’s authority,” he said, “but that court and its allies in the global bureaucracy have appointed themselves judge and jury and executioner of the international order.”

His case for the country: “To submit to the sterile vision of radical judges or soulless global bureaucrats would be to betray who we are.”

Then he quoted the Roman general Pompey: “Stop quoting laws to men with swords.”
stories.pull_quote: Americans have never agreed to submit to the ICC’s authority.

record.label: Rubio at the Federalist Society’s 2026 National Lawyers Convention: “Americans have never agreed to submit to the ICC’s authority, but that court and its allies in the global bureaucracy have appointed themselves judge and jury and executioner of the international order”; “To submit to the sterile vision of radical judges or soulless global bureaucrats would be to betray who we are”; Pompey: “Stop quoting laws to men with swords”

Speech at the Mayflower Hotel Nov. 13; “his first prepared remarks since Republicans were routed in the midterm elections”; U.S. sanctions on the ICC take effect in April unless supporters reach an agreement with Washington

stories.headline: March: Delta’s CEO Said Amazon Leo Is “the Best, Fastest and Most Cost-Effective Technology Available.”
stories.headline_now: Now: Installs Start in 2028. United Has Starlink on 697 Planes.
stories.deck: Ed Bastian is “very confident in our decision.” Musk’s reply to the “long game” talk: “I found a pic of ‘the long game.’”
stories.body:
March 31, Delta picked Amazon’s Leo satellite Wi-Fi over Elon Musk’s Starlink. CEO Ed Bastian said it “gives us the best, fastest and most cost-effective technology available.”

The catch: installs start in 2028, on an initial 500 planes.

Last Thursday, on Bloomberg, Bastian stood by it. Leo is “coming to the skies here relatively soon, over the next 18 months,” he said, and he’s “very confident in our decision.”

United, meanwhile, has 697 Starlink-equipped aircraft, covering 51% of its daily flights, Simple Flying reports.

Musk’s review: “I found a pic of ‘the long game.’”

stories.headline: Musk Went Over the Starship SpaceX Just Caught. His Verdict: Ship 42 “Could Probably Be Reflown.”
stories.deck: A day after the first tower catch, he checked the heat shield: “Overall, it looks great.” Next up: a Starship V4 about 70 meters long.
stories.body:
A day after SpaceX caught a Starship upper stage with its tower for the first time, Elon Musk was at the pad going over Ship 42.

“Overall, it looks great. The engines look great too,” he posted Sunday. “Ship 42 could probably be reflown with a few weeks of refurbishment.” SpaceX has never reflown a ship, Teslarati notes.

His honest caveat: “many small fixes are needed to achieve immediate reusability (like an airplane).”

Then he went bigger. “Starship V4 will be ~70m long,” he wrote, with nine engines and more than 60% more propellant.
stories.pull_quote: Ship 42 could probably be reflown with a few weeks of refurbishment.

record.label: Musk, 5:20 p.m. ET: “I was going over the whole Starship heat shield earlier today. Overall, it looks great. The engines look great too. Ship 42 could probably be reflown with a few weeks of refurbishment”; “many small fixes are needed to achieve immediate reusability (like an airplane)”
Musk, 8:33 p.m. ET: “Starship V4 will be ~70m long, which is roughly a 40% length increase and allows >60% more propellant load”; engine count raised to 9 with 3 more Raptor-Vacuum engines
Musk spent part of Sunday at the pad inspecting the ship caught Saturday; “SpaceX has never reflown a ship”; current V3 ship about 52 meters
Musk seen on a platform at the pad inspecting Ship 42’s heat shield tiles; ship moved back to Production for further inspection
“SpaceX has yet to reuse a Ship, as it had not caught one during a mission until Saturday”

stories.headline: 2014: NASA Picked Boeing at Up to $4.2 Billion and SpaceX at $2.6 Billion to Fly Astronauts.
stories.headline_now: 2026: Crew Dragon Is “the Only Currently Operational U.S. Astronaut Ferry Ship.”
stories.deck: Starliner’s 2024 crew flight left two astronauts on the station for more than nine months. A Crew Dragon brought them home. Musk: “Yup.”
stories.body:
Sept. 16, 2014, NASA picked two companies to fly astronauts to the space station: Boeing, with a maximum contract value of $4.2 billion, and SpaceX, at $2.6 billion.

Twelve years later, SpaceX’s Crew Dragon is “the only currently operational U.S. astronaut ferry ship,” Spaceflight Now reports.

Starliner’s first crewed flight, in 2024, suffered propulsion failures. Butch Wilmore and Sunita Williams stayed aboard the station more than nine months and rode home on a Crew Dragon. Starliner’s next crewed flight is planned for 2028.

Musk’s review of the comparison: “Yup.”
stories.pull_quote: SpaceX’s Crew Dragon capsule is the only currently operational U.S. astronaut ferry ship.

Uncrewed Starliner-1 cargo flight planned for the December 2026/January 2027 timeframe; “A crewed Starliner-2 mission is planned for 2028”
“SpaceX will get $2.6 billion and Boeing will receive $4.2 billion, officials said”

stories.headline: Tesla’s Cybercab Costs $29,990 Plus $299 a Month. Musk’s Own Review of the Fee: “Too High.”
stories.deck: Select customers can now pre-order the steering-wheel-free two-seater for personal use. The boss says the monthly charge should be more like $115.
stories.body:
Tesla opened invite-only Cybercab pre-orders “for personal use” on Friday: $29,990, plus a mandatory $299-a-month Autonomy Subscription, The Verge reports. Buyers must take delivery in one of a handful of Texas cities, and the car runs only inside Robotaxi service areas. Estimated delivery: December.

Tech reviewer Marques Brownlee posted the fine print. Hours later, Musk agreed with the gripe.

“The monthly fee is too high,” he wrote. It “should match the cost of Tesla FSD and connectivity for other models, which is more like ~$115/month.”

A CEO calling his own price too high. Noted.
stories.pull_quote: The monthly fee is too high.

record.label: Musk, 1:38 a.m. ET, replying to Marques Brownlee: “It will be available nationwide, as we receive regulatory approval. But the monthly fee is too high. Should match the cost of Tesla FSD and connectivity for other models, which is more like ~$115/month.”
Brownlee, 8:50 p.m. ET: invite only; must accept delivery in Texas; only operates in existing geofenced areas; monthly subscription
Pre-orders announced Friday evening; $29,990; $299 a month; delivery in a handful of Texas cities; geofenced; estimated December 2026

stories.headline: “Did Democrats Screw This Up?” Katherine Clark, Next in Line for Majority Leader: “Yes.”
stories.deck: Eleven House Democrats missed the Hegseth impeachment vote. The Massachusetts Democrat owned it on WCVB, then promised to haul in Jensen Huang.
stories.body:
Rep. Katherine Clark of Massachusetts, poised to become the first woman to serve as House majority leader, sat down with WCVB’s On The Record. The topic: the Hegseth impeachment vote 11 Democrats missed.

“Did Democrats screw this up?”

“Yes,” Clark said. “You know, we have to take accountability for that.”

ABC News did the math: with all 11 there, the motion could have failed 215-211.

Next on her list: “We will be bringing in Jensen Huang.” CNN’s sources say the intelligence on the woman in that story “does not prove that she was acting as a spy.”
stories.pull_quote: Yes. You know, we have to take accountability for that.

record.label: Clark on WCVB’s On The Record: asked “Did Democrats screw this up?”, she said “Yes. You know, we have to take accountability for that”; Democrats will “absolutely” investigate Huang: “So we will be bringing in Jensen Huang. We will be investigating this fully”
11 Democrats missed the vote; held open 29 minutes; with all 11, the motion “could have been defeated 215-211”; several blamed traffic
Roll Call 317, H. Res. 1655, motion to refer: 211-204; Democrats 0-203 with 11 not voting

stories.headline: Senate Republicans’ Lame-Duck Mission: Confirm Trump’s Judges. 23 Are Pending. The Next Vote Is Today.
stories.deck: Thune: “Our work will have a generational effect.” The White House expects every pending nominee confirmed this year, even as a few GOP senators dig in.
stories.body:
Democrats take the Senate in January. Senate Republicans are putting judges first.

Fifty-seven Trump judges have been confirmed this term, 23 nominees are pending, and a vote is set for Monday on Daniel Domenico for the 10th Circuit, Reuters reports. The White House: “We expect all judicial nominees pending in the Senate to be confirmed this year.”

Majority Leader John Thune says the pace from nomination to confirmation is the fastest since Reagan. “Our work will have a generational effect.”

The holdouts are Republican: outgoing Sens. Thom Tillis and John Cornyn have signaled they may block some picks.

stories.headline: “Mechazilla Catches Starship!” For the First Time Ever, the Ship Came Home From Orbit Into the Tower’s Arms
stories.deck: After about 22 hours in space, Ship 42 broke through the clouds over Starbase and eased into the chopsticks. Musk: “I hugged ship 42 upon its return.”
stories.body:
Saturday around 4:20 p.m. ET, after about 22 hours in space, Ship 42 broke through the clouds over Starbase, Texas, flipped upright and eased into the waiting arms of the launch tower.

“Mechazilla catches Starship!” SpaceX posted. It was the first catch ever of a Starship upper stage. NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman: “It was almost magic.”

The booster was lost Friday after its catch was called off, so the full double catch Musk called “more likely than not” in October still waits. Engineers are investigating.

Musk’s review: “I hugged ship 42 upon its return.”
stories.pull_quote: Mechazilla catches Starship! Congratulations to the entire SpaceX team on this incredible achievement!

record.label: SpaceX, 4:21 p.m. ET: “Mechazilla catches Starship! Congratulations to the entire SpaceX team on this incredible achievement!”
First successful catch of the Starship vehicle itself by the “Mechazilla” tower, around 4:20 p.m. ET; booster aborted its catch and detonated over the Gulf; SpaceX still determining the cause

Caught by the “chopstick arms” about 22 hours after launch; “the first-ever capture of a Starship flying back from space”; 14 laps of Earth; Isaacman on X: “It was almost magic”; Kate Tice on the booster’s engines stopping too soon
Musk, 7:35 p.m. ET: “I hugged ship 42 upon its return”

Musk announced the plan to catch both stages on Flight 15 during the Q3 call; “more likely than not”

stories.headline: America’s Skies Shut Down Over “1980s Little Copper Lines.” Duffy: “This Is an Emergency.”
stories.deck: Friday’s ground stop hit during a copper-to-fiber upgrade. Speaker Johnson on Trump and Duffy: “They’ve been sounding the alarm.”
stories.body:
Friday, the FAA grounded every flight in America, the longest halt in U.S. departures since 9/11, CNBC reports.

Secretary Sean Duffy says a contractor was swapping old copper lines for fiber when a router flooded the system with more than 1,000 connection attempts every four to five seconds, disrupting communications and radar. The exact fault is still unknown.

“We use 1980s little copper lines,” Duffy said. He wants $50 billion.

Some Democrats note only $4.3 billion of 2025’s $12.5 billion is obligated. DHS chief Markwayne Mullin: “This is what happens when Congress kicks the can down the road.”

stories.headline: Somerville Votes 10-1 to Divest Over “Israel and Palestine.” The Lone No: “It Makes Us Feel Unsafe.”
stories.deck: Councilor Kristen Strezo spoke for her Jewish community and invoked Kristallnacht as chants rose outside. The ordinance passed with a veto-proof majority.
stories.body:
Thursday night, the Somerville City Council voted 10-1 to keep city money from companies tied to violations of international humanitarian law, naming those operating in “Israel and Palestine,” JTA reports.

The lone no: Councilor Kristen Strezo. Speaking for her Jewish community, she said the ordinance “makes us feel targeted. It makes us feel unsafe. It makes us feel unwelcome.”

“A few years before Kristallnacht, the Nazis worked to deter the public from shopping at Jewish businesses,” she said. “Their efforts started in moments like tonight.”

Outside, chants rose over her speech. The measure is final.
stories.pull_quote: This ordinance will do nothing to solve the real conflict in the Middle East.

stories.headline: Starship Is in Orbit, Circling Earth “Every ~90 Minutes.” Today It Tries to Come Home to the Tower.
stories.deck: Flight 15 put 26 Starlink V3 satellites in orbit. The booster catch was called off. Overnight, SpaceX said the ship and heatshield are “healthy.”
stories.body:
Elon Musk’s Starship lifted off from Starbase, Texas, Friday evening on Flight 15 and reached orbit for the second time ever. “We’ve got a nominal orbit insertion,” SpaceX’s Dan Huot said on the webcast.

It deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites. The Super Heavy booster’s tower catch was called off, and it splashed down in the Gulf instead.

Overnight, SpaceX said the ship and its heatshield are “healthy.” Musk: “Starship is traveling around the world every ~90 minutes right now.”

If all stays healthy, the ship attempts the first-ever tower catch of a Starship upper stage around 4:20 p.m. ET today.

stories.headline: The Supreme Court Will Decide Whether Trump Can Suspend Asylum at the Southern Border
stories.deck: The justices took up the administration’s appeal Friday. Lower courts ruled against the policy, but it stays in place while the case goes on.
stories.body:
The Supreme Court agreed Friday to decide whether President Trump can suspend access to asylum for migrants at the U.S.-Mexico border, SCOTUSblog reports.

The policy began with a Jan. 20, 2025, proclamation declaring that “an invasion is ongoing at the southern border.” A district judge ruled against it, and a D.C. Circuit panel largely agreed. The appeals court put its ruling on hold, so the restrictions remain.

Solicitor General D. John Sauer told the justices the proclamation “rests on a commonsense understanding of the President’s inherent and delegated powers to exclude aliens.”

Now the justices decide.

A New York Times news analysis on Trump’s “chaotic greatest hits” said he called into the premiere of a C-SPAN show “apparently without notice.”

Early Wednesday, Trump posted that it was “a fully scheduled call, as a favor to C-Span, set up through White House Communications.”

stories.headline: October: She Wanted Young Republicans to Fear “a Ton of Problems.”
stories.headline_now: November, After Trump Called for a DOJ Look: “Coordinated Play.”
stories.deck: Sen. Elissa Slotkin wanted a “deterrence message” sent to students thinking about Trump administration jobs. Now the message has a return address.
stories.body:
Oct. 13, at the University of Chicago, Sen. Elissa Slotkin said she wanted students weighing Trump administration jobs to think, “Lord, that might be buying myself a ton of problems.” Her words: “I want that deterrence message.”

This weekend, President Trump ordered the Justice Department to look into those remarks. Slotkin says he “really ramped up his coordinated play,” and her lawyer, Preet Bharara, wrote to DOJ.

Her defense now: “If you’re not violating the law — no problem.”

DOJ’s reply: “public service should not be met with threats of retribution.”

Deterrence reads differently from the other side.

then.text: I want them to be like, Lord, that might be buying myself a ton of problems that I don't want, and so let me avoid participating in that. I want that deterrence message.
then.source_name: Fox News, quoting her University of Chicago remarks
then.who: Sen. Elissa Slotkin (D-Mich.), University of Chicago

now.text: A couple weeks ago, I talked about how anyone who is violating the law or misusing taxpayer dollars should be held accountable... If you're not violating the law — no problem.
now.source_name: Fox News, quoting her video response
now.who: Sen. Elissa Slotkin (D-Mich.), video posted Monday

stories.headline: 2022: Wu Pulled Seven-Unit Buildings Into Her Affordable-Housing Rules. “Every Tool.”
stories.headline_now: Since: Eight Units Permitted. Now She Wants the Trigger Back at 10.
stories.deck: Before the change, Boston averaged 144 permitted units a year in seven-to-nine-unit projects, the city’s housing chief says. Since it took effect: eight.
stories.body:
Dec. 15, 2022: Mayor Michelle Wu proposed that projects of seven or more units, down from 10, help fund affordable housing, and raised the required affordable share. “We are using every tool that the City has,” she said. It took effect Oct. 1, 2024.

Boston used to average 144 permitted units a year in seven-to-nine-unit projects, her housing chief told GBH. Since the change: eight.

This week Wu proposed raising the trigger back to 10 for now and cutting a condo fee, blaming headwinds “exacerbated by federal actions.” High interest rates and building costs, GBH notes, are also slowing construction.
stories.pull_quote: We are using every tool that the City has to urgently address Boston’s housing crisis

then.text: We are using every tool that the City has to urgently address Boston's housing crisis
then.who: Boston Mayor Michelle Wu

now.text: In the face of continued economic headwinds exacerbated by federal actions, we are making targeted adjustments to help more projects move forward and create more affordability
now.who: Boston Mayor Michelle Wu

record.label: Wu proposes lowering the inclusionary threshold from 10 to seven units and raising the rental affordable share from 13% to 20%: “We are using every tool that the City has to urgently address Boston’s housing crisis”

Wu proposes raising the minimum project size from seven to 10 units temporarily and cutting the condo payment-in-lieu fee from 75% to 50%; housing chief Sheila Dillon: 144 permitted units a year with seven to nine units in the four years before the change, only eight since
City page: changes in effect October 2024 lowered the trigger from ten to seven units and raised the income-restricted share to 17–20%

stories.headline: 56% Voted to Keep Girls’ Sports for Girls. Jayapal: “We’re Going to Start Planning for How We Overturn These.”
stories.deck: Washington’s party chair says “the fight over I-638 is just beginning.” In Colorado, the governor-elect talks “adjustments.” Republicans: No Kings.
stories.body:
Washington voters passed Initiative 638 with about 56 percent. Starting Dec. 3, it keeps students it defines as biologically male off girls’ K-12 teams.

Election night, Rep. Pramila Jayapal said: “We are going to take our state back. We’re going to start planning for how we overturn these bad initiatives.” The state Democratic chair says “the fight over I-638 is just beginning” and backs a court challenge.

In Colorado, which passed a similar measure, Gov.-elect Phil Weiser says legislators can ask “what are the adjustments that need to be added.”

Voters spoke. Some politicians are still talking.
stories.pull_quote: If the Democrats truly believe there should be ‘No Kings’ in America, it is time they take their own advice.

stories.headline: A New Democrat Flipped a Trump Seat. He Says Party Elders Promised Him “a Living Hell” Unless He Backs Jeffries.
stories.deck: Rep.-elect Don Leonard of Ohio hasn’t been sworn in. He says he already got the welcome speech. He didn’t name who gave it.
stories.body:
Don Leonard, an Ohio State city-planning professor, flipped Ohio’s 15th District last week, beating Republican Rep. Mike Carey by more than six points in a seat Trump carried by about 10.

In an Instagram video, Leonard says senior House Democrats told him that holding back his vote for Hakeem Jeffries as speaker would mean “making my life a living hell for the next two years here in Washington” and losing his next election. He did not name them.

His conditions include ending Citizens United and U.S. support for the Iran war.

The party of “democracy” has a whip count.

stories.headline: SpaceX Posted Notice of a $24 Billion Supercomputer. The Governor-Elect Promised “a Ban.”
stories.deck: A gas-fired plant and “super-compute facility” on about 444 acres in Starbase. Tax breaks go before the city on Dec. 9.
stories.body:
Monday, Starbase posted notice of a Dec. 9 hearing: SpaceX proposes a “gas-fired power plant and super-compute facility” on about 444 acres, with estimated capital investment of $24 billion. The city will consider a tax abatement.

The Texas Tribune reports the land was de-annexed from Brownsville earlier this year after SpaceX offered $220 million for water and wastewater projects. Brownsville’s 90-day data-center moratorium took effect last week.

Oct. 22, Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa promised “a moratorium — a ban — on all data center approvals until laws can be passed by the Legislature to protect Texans.” She takes office Jan. 19.

stories.headline: Clavicular Says the Dictionaries Crowned His Words and Sneaker Ads Copy Him, Asks Who Had a More Influential Year
stories.deck: His exhibit: a Skechers subway poster. Dictionary.com picked “maxxing.” Collins picked “mogging.” Neither names him.
stories.body:
Clavicular has filed his year-end review. “First, they mock you. Then the various dictionaries declare your words the words of the years,” he posted at 2:46 p.m. ET Wednesday. “Name a creator who had a more influential year than me?”

The dictionaries are real. Dictionary.com picked “maxxing” on Oct. 25, with looksmaxxing among its examples. Collins picked “mogging” on Nov. 3. Neither names him.

He also says marketers copy him “to sell sneakers.” His evidence: a Skechers subway poster starring a cartoon man in a navy jacket. Visible slogans: “Arch Fit” and “Slip-ins.”

Oxford rules Dec. 1.

stories.headline: CobbRuvs Declares “Miami Baby, Here I Come,” Talks Fight Terms With Drago, Then Rules Tim Hortons Tastes Like Bologna
stories.deck: A seven-and-a-half-hour Toronto send-off: a Florida game plan, a live video call, a closed CN Tower and a sandwich verdict.
stories.body: CobbRuvs announced his next chapter from a Toronto high-rise, Coca-Cola in hand and nu-metal on the TV: “Miami baby, here I come.” He says he’ll fly out by Thursday at the latest, catch his brother there and walk the city with a selfie stick. Then he got Drago on a live video call to talk terms for a proposed fight. Drago pitched a streamable MMA-gym bout; nothing was settled. His Toronto goodbye found the CN Tower closed. At Tim Hortons he offered to pay, then ruled on the sandwich: “It smells and tastes like bologna. Welcome to Canada.”
stories.pull_quote: It smells and tastes like bologna. Welcome to Canada.

record.date_label: Tuesday, Nov. 17, 6:24 p.m. ET to about 1:56 a.m. ET Wednesday, Nov. 18 (7 hours, 31 minutes)
record.label: A Toronto apartment stream and farewell walk. Livestream 138457024. The VOD had 11,330 views at about 2:04 a.m. ET, and he had 30,984 followers. The desk logged a live high of about 2,199 viewers around midnight ET. Cold approaches: 0; he says those are scheduled for Miami. Private people, including a guest and shop staff, are not named or shown.

The announcement: “Miami baby, here I come.” He said he has been “manifesting this,” and that he’s doing it “not only for me, I’m doing it for you guys.” On the plan: “We’re hitting Miami.” He said he would meet his brother there. He promised to walk Miami with his selfie stick: “It might not be good, but we gonna do it.”
He started a one-way flight search for the next day and said he would be there “by Thursday by the latest.” A completed ticket purchase never showed up on the tape.

A live video call with Drago, who appeared on camera in a fursuit head. CobbRuvs: “I called you out, so you get to pick how you want to fight me.” Drago said he would “prefer to do this in a way where it benefits both of us the most” and proposed an MMA-gym bout: “you can stream it.” No date, venue or terms were settled. CobbRuvs also apologized on the call for an earlier callout.
“Shout out to looksmax, and that was a fun little era. Now it’s back to content… I’m coming to Miami with my selfie stick.”

“We’re doing a little Toronto goodbye, gentlemen.” He wanted to go into the CN Tower but learned it closes at 11, with the night already near midnight. He asked chat to pick the Bahamas or Cancun after Miami.

At Tim Hortons, which he pitched as “what Canada’s built off,” he offered to pay: “whatever you want, man, it’s on me.” Back on the couch, the beef-sandwich review: the bread is “not bad,” and he’d want “chipotle mayonnaise or maybe like an aioli.” Verdict: “It smells like a hot dog… no, it’s not hot dog, it’s bologna. It smells and tastes like bologna. Welcome to Canada.”
Late in the night: “I’m going home.” There was no formal good-night; the stream ended at about 1:56 a.m. ET.

share.caption: MIAMI BABY, HERE I COME.

stories.headline: Hexumlite Went Home to London, Ky., His “Spawn Point,” for 24 Approaches, a Walmart Blitz and Hoops Under the Lights
stories.deck: The light triad sweater’s homecoming: the Speedway where he says it all started, Growler at Walmart and a reunion on the court.
stories.body: Hexumlite took the light triad sweater home. In London, Ky., he said, “This is my hometown. This is my spawn point.” He stopped at the Speedway where, he said, he filmed his first IRL video. At Walmart he announced, “We’re taking the Walmart pill and the dog pill at the same time,” and worked the aisles: 13 approaches there, 24 on the night, zero confirmed numbers by the desk’s read. He called cold approaching “a sport” and himself “the Michael Jordan.” An old basketball teammate walked up, and they played under the lights. His verdict: “a really wholesome stream.”

Kick’s public API showed 10,862 VOD views at about 9:22 p.m. ET; the desk’s logged live high was 1,916 viewers at about 6:00 p.m. ET. He wore the same American-flag sweater, which he said was his fifth day in a row. Private people, including the women he approached and his old teammate, are not named or shown.
Faster-whisper, 1:37: “This is my hometown. This is my spawn point.” Locals in the lot brought up the first KFC in Corbin and the moonbow at Cumberland Falls. “I wish I wasn’t leaving tomorrow.”

At a Speedway he called “literally the place where I filmed my first IRL video,” about a year ago. He told people inside he was born and raised in London, then walked past the old movie theater and arcade from his teenage years.

Into Walmart with Growler: “We’re taking the Walmart pill and the dog pill at the same time.” On the desk’s best read, 13 approaches in the aisles, including the cashier, and none ended with a confirmed number. To chat: “Why can’t I pull a decent looking girl?” He called cold approaching “a sport” and himself “the Michael Jordan,” and asked fans for a video of his year of approaches, “because a lot of them were like off cam too.”

An old basketball teammate walked up in Walmart. They drove past First Baptist, where he “used to hoop… every day,” to the courts by the farmer’s market and played first-to-five under the lights as more locals joined. At 2:42:48: “It’s actually been a really wholesome stream. I’m glad I did that.”
More approaches in the lot, then McAlister’s, where he ordered a Reuben with no sauce. Chat asked about the next New York meetup; he said he wanted another one.
24 initiated approaches, 0 confirmed numbers or Instagrams, at least 8 clear rejections. Two number asks ended with nothing confirmed on tape. These are the desk’s counts, not an official tally.
Back in the Texas Roadhouse lot, the crew said goodbye to the old teammate and headed out toward Lexington. The stream ended at about 8:32 p.m. ET.

stories.headline: Hexumlite Took His “Light Triad Fit” to Tennessee Tech, Spilled the Raw Milk and Got a Campus Police Check
stories.deck: A flag sweater, three-inch height inserts, Growler on a leash and a meetup with a longtime follower, then ice cream at Poppie’s.
stories.body: Hexumlite took his road trip to Tennessee Tech in what he called his “light triad fit”: an American-flag sweater, three-inch height inserts and Growler on a leash. Two early approaches in the stadium lot went nowhere. Then the longtime follower he had come to meet, known on stream as “Big 200,” walked up with gifts. He offered her raw milk and promptly spilled it: “Damn, I spilled all the raw milk guys.” A campus police officer stopped them over suspected soliciting, then let them keep walking. Ice cream at Poppie’s followed. Next, he says: maybe Memphis.
stories.pull_quote: Damn, I spilled all the raw milk guys.

record.date_label: Monday, Nov. 16, 3:13:01 p.m. ET to about 4:57:03 p.m. ET (1 hour, 44 minutes, 2 seconds)
record.label: A daytime IRL walk across the Tennessee Tech campus in Cookeville, Tenn. Official Kick duration 6,242,000 ms. IRL; English. Livestream 138236480. Kick’s public API showed 7,846 VOD views as of 5:07 p.m. ET and 15,034 followers at the same check. Cold approaches: 3 initiated, 0 confirmed contacts, by FNN’s read of the tape. The women he approached and the woman he came to meet are not named or shown.

“We are here at Tennessee Tech. It’s a pretty nice spot… It’s like fall weather. I got the light triad fit on.” He said he looked “like relationship material,” then listed the fit: three-inch height inserts, the “light triad sweater,” and Growler. Faster-whisper.
Two approaches in the stadium parking lot, both built around a bit about whether to break up with his girlfriend. No number or Instagram was taken; the group said, “okay, no worries.”
The meetup: “Yo, this is… big 200. Yo, what’s up?” She arrived with gifts and a skateboard. Nickname used on stream by both of them; her name is not printed.
At his car, he offered raw milk from a jug and spilled it: “Damn, I spilled all the raw milk guys.” He told her it was “fine” and “don’t be sorry.”

In a campus quad, a police officer walked up. On the desk’s best listen, the question was whether they were soliciting. They said they were not asking people for anything and were allowed to keep walking. No one was accused of anything on tape.
Into the campus food court, past a Taco Bell kiosk, to Poppie’s Ice Cream Shoppe. He switched his order to “the coffee one.” He let a woman pet Growler: “Please pet him.”

On Clavicular, during a talk about greatness: “even people like clav and these types were like thought it’s weird or people didn’t like them until you know their greatness could be communicated and like that success actually happened.”
Back at the lot, she left for class. He said they were “thinking about going to Memphis after this.” Sign-off at 1:43:50: “Alright well I’ll see you guys I’m gonna hop off here.”

stories.headline: CobbRuvs’ First Daytime Toronto Stream: A Haircut He Roasted, $40 in a Stranger’s Tank and His First-Ever Oxtail
stories.deck: Nine hours in the 6: King Street “characters,” a gas-station vlog, a pot-roast verdict at Miss Likklemore’s and a banana-milk walk home.
stories.body: CobbRuvs finally took Toronto in daylight, and it became a nine-hour marathon. He opened by roasting his fresh haircut, calling it a “bowl cut” before promising, “give it a few days, it’ll look better.” Then he headed for King Street: “We gotta make characters. Interaction, storyline.” A gas-station vlog ended with $40 in a man’s tank. At Miss Likklemore’s he reviewed his first-ever oxtail: the meat “tastes like your mother’s pot roast,” and “this is so awesome.” Street interviews followed, then a snack run for banana milk and peanut-butter crackers on the cold walk home. Sign-off: “See you tomorrow.”
stories.pull_quote: It’s the first time I’ve had oxtail. Oh my god, this is so awesome.

stories.headline: Burt Bronx Says He Canceled Salvo’s Flight Home Mid-Fight. Ted Begged. An Hour Later: “I Did Fix It, Guys.”
stories.deck: Skankfest Day 3 in an orange jumpsuit: a rain delay, fan photos, a canceled-ticket confession and a scramble to save Ted’s flight.
stories.body: Skankfest Day 3 brought rain, the orange INMATE jumpsuit and a confession. Ted asked on camera whether Salvo’s flight home had “been altered.” Burt said he had “purposely canceled his ticket” on the United app during Saturday’s hotel-room fight, hoping Salvo would find out at the airport “as an unfortunate surprise.” His travel advice: Salvo “can just walk home to Philly.” Ted pleaded: “I don’t want him to hate us forever for this.” Then Ted told chat Salvo said he was canceling Ted’s flight next. After an hour of damage control, Burt announced: “I did fix it, guys.”
stories.pull_quote: I didn’t intend on making an enemy of this guy.

stories.headline: Hexumlite Hit Broadway With Growler, Declared Himself “Blue Collar Light,” Then Surrendered to the Nashville Cold
stories.deck: A 1-hour, 53-minute Nashville walk: a boot shop, a rooftop bar with the skyline, two numbers by FNN’s count, and Memphis tomorrow.
stories.body: Hexumlite’s road trip finally reached Broadway. Hood up, Growler on the leash, he announced: “I’m in Nashville, guys. Finally back on the road trip.” He rolled out a new identity, “blue collar light,” and greeted men on the sidewalk accordingly. He shopped steel-toe boots, then rode up to a new rooftop bar with the Nashville skyline behind him. FNN counted 13 attempts and two phone numbers. Then the cold won: “Sometimes in life, you just got to bitch out.” From the car, he said he signed with Duel, is headed to Memphis tomorrow and is done with his girlfriend.

stories.headline: Clavicular Says His Girlfriend Shaved Her Head to Protect His Pores. He Called It “Bare Minimum.”
stories.deck: A now-deleted post cited “comedogenic hair-product residue.” Ninety minutes later, to the haters: “She still looks great.”
stories.body:
Sunday at 8:08 p.m. ET, Clavicular unveiled a skin-care protocol: “Nocturnal facial contact with a woman’s hair may expose skin to comedogenic hair-product residue, causing acne. My girlfriend in an attempt to aid me in my looksmaxing journey shaved all of her hair off. Very loving gesture, bare minimum.”

The post is gone. “Ok she wanted me to delete it, but fuck that was going to be the best bait in twitter history.” To the critics: “Female hair products build up and clog pores. She still looks great.” Lacy, on stream: “What the fuck.” His reply to Lacy: “Based.”
stories.pull_quote: Nocturnal facial contact with a woman’s hair may expose skin to comedogenic hair-product residue, causing acne.

image.alt: Clavicular shirtless in a gym, posing in front of weight machines
image.caption: Clavicular in “The mog,” the 11-second gym clip he posted Sunday night between defenses of the shave.

share.caption: BARE MINIMUM.

stories.headline: Salvo Called Burt Bronx a “Side Character.” Burt Said He’s “Not Welcome,” Then Wore an Orange Jumpsuit to Skankfest
stories.deck: A 4-hour, 10-minute New Orleans tape: an hour-long hotel-room dressing-down, Ted in tears, an eviction and a pause at the ballroom door.
stories.body: Burt Bronx’s Sunday afternoon stream became a prestige drama. In a New Orleans hotel room, Salvo spent the better part of an hour dressing him down. Salvo, at one point: “You’re a side character.” Burt sat still: “I’m just kind of letting him cook.” Ted, near tears: “You guys are breaking my heart.” Then Burt ruled: “You’re not welcome in this hotel room anymore.” Ted, crying: “I’m sorry for everything.” Burt changed into an orange prison-style jumpsuit, discovered on the Uber ride that Salvo had unfollowed him, and paused at the ballroom door: “We will be back after this.”
stories.pull_quote: I’m kind of curious to see what else he has to say, so I’m just kind of letting him cook.

stories.headline: HeelMike Coached The Myth From Ringside, Then Got Into an Afterparty as Mario: “I Can’t Believe That Just Worked”
stories.deck: A 3-hour, 50-minute San Diego tape: a warehouse boxing night, nine fights for The Myth, “Mario was invited” and a door that let Mario in.
stories.body: HeelMike’s birthday reached its boxing chapter. At a San Diego warehouse fight night under an “ARK” banner, he appointed himself coach of The Myth and issued instructions from ringside: “Remember everything I taught you, myth.” The Myth fought nine people. His review: “it’s kind of badass.” Asked about an invitation, he answered in character: “Mario was invited.” Then came an afterparty with a line at the door. By his account, he walked up in the Mario cap and was told, “you’re good.” His statement: “Holy shit. I can’t believe that just worked.” At the drop-off: “they’re actually my friends.”

stories.headline: Ted Rode Burt Bronx Around a Hotel Bed as “Seabiscuit.” Then Matan Picked Up for the First Time in Eight Months.
stories.deck: A 2-hour, 1-minute New Orleans hotel tape: a mogging mission, a laptop slam, a call to Matan and a bar run that died on the bed.
stories.body: Skankfest Day 2 had one more session in it. At 2:39 a.m. ET, Burt Bronx and Ted went live from their New Orleans hotel room. Chat asked Ted to ride Burt around the bed like a horse to “mog” Frank. Ted saddled up: “Come on, Seabiscuit… We’re mogging Frank.” A donated song Ted called “Frank-coded” got the laptop slammed; it survived. Then Burt dialed Matan, who, he says, last answered March 3: “Matan, it’s Burt.” The call closed with “All right, Burt, enjoy your night.” The bar run died on the bed. Sign-off: “I’ll see you guys then.”
stories.pull_quote: Come on, Seabiscuit. Come on, Seabiscuit. We’re mogging Frank.

stories.body: HeelMike spent Saturday night in San Diego in a white Mario cap and denied the plumber outright: “Who the fuck is Mario? It’s a me Mike.” It ran all night. He told chat to hold the camera still: “I just want to look big.” At a restaurant, he says, an elderly couple asked why they had never heard of him. He set the record straight: “I stream because I love being a Super Mega Star Ultra mega famous.” Then the rebuttal: “Why the fuck would a fifty year old couple know who [HeelMike] is?”

stories.headline: Burt Bronx Rode the Skankfest Ferris Wheel Yelling “We’re Going to Die,” Then Shane Gillis Said No Photos
stories.deck: The late Day 2 session: Luis J. Gomez walks by, a $1,200 prize for Salvo, a cinematic bridge and a pause before Legion of Skanks.
stories.body: Skankfest Day 2 got a night shift. Burt Bronx and Ted came back live from Mardi Gras World at 7:17 p.m. ET, and within a minute Luis J. Gomez walked right by. Salvo, by their account, had won a $1,200 prize in an off-stream funny-story contest. On the Ferris wheel, Burt filed his report: “We’re going to die.” Then: “Does it look cinematic?” Ted says he punched Shane Gillis on the arm and asked for a photo; Shane’s answer, as Ted tells it: “Nah, no photos.” At the Legion of Skanks door: “Okay, guys, we’ll be back.”

stories.deck: Day 2 of 3: a New Orleans hotel room, Salvo’s arrival, Mardi Gras World, a booth fighting game and a pause at the door of a show they couldn’t stream.
stories.body: Skankfest Day 2 finally got its delegation. Burt Bronx and Ted spent more than four hours in a New Orleans hotel room, where Burt secured Comic-Con tickets for July and survived one round of on-stream vomiting, until Salvo walked in: “I’m not Ted’s man… I’m Ted’s friend.” Then came the Uber to Mardi Gras World, a Legion of Skanks hoodie found on the grounds and a hello with Luis J. Gomez. Ted rode the mechanical bull in an orange Flyers jersey. “Damn, Ted, you’re doing great.” At the tent door, they paused as promised: “Stream, we will be back.”

record.label: Ted reminded chat that he “ended the stream last night sitting in Burt’s carry-on.” He argued that Ice Poseidon’s Safe Zone was a bad bet for Burt’s time: “over a hundred and fifty people got eliminated in the first twenty four hours.” Neither had really eaten beyond leftover chicken wings, and they asked chat to flag whether Kill Tony or Tony Hinchcliffe was doing anything at the festival. Kick captions.
record.source: Kick VOD, Burt Bronx, “BURT BRONX + TED: SKANKFEST DAY 2 OF 3”

record.label: Burt said he “got all [the] Comic-Con tickets” for July. Asked by chat for a negative about Ted, he offered: “you’re not as good at skateboard as you think you are and you come off as a skateboarding poser.” Then: “Salvo’s on his way anyway… he just landed.” Kick captions.
record.source: Kick VOD, Burt Bronx, “BURT BRONX + TED: SKANKFEST DAY 2 OF 3”

record.label: Burt got sick on stream; the vomit was audible. Ted: “you guys got to hear all that.” A pop-culture detour followed, and chat’s verdict on Burt’s alignment came back “Ravenclaw with a strong Slytherin overlap.” Kick captions.
record.source: Kick VOD, Burt Bronx, “BURT BRONX + TED: SKANKFEST DAY 2 OF 3”

record.label: Salvo arrived: “Big bird, what’s going on? We’re streaming right now, guys… special guest.” Salvo: “I’m not Ted’s man… I’m Ted’s friend and I’m your friend too.” Burt read the day’s plan: a 5 p.m. local show at the Forbidden Apothecary, Legion of Skanks around 8 p.m., and a late Apothecary show around 11 p.m. The rule, as they explained it: “When we’re under the tents we’re not allowed to livestream, but we can get like fans’ reactions… they’re gonna kick us out if we stream a stand-up set.” The night plan: “We’re going to Bourbon Street tonight, chat… we’re having the time of our life and there’s nothing you all can do about it except sit back and enjoy.” Kick captions, proper names cleaned up.
record.source: Kick VOD, Burt Bronx, “BURT BRONX + TED: SKANKFEST DAY 2 OF 3”

record.label: Running late for their 4:30 p.m. local target, they took an Uber, telling the driver about “a couple travel days from hell.” Salvo still has no Twitter; Burt told him to make one tonight. Kick captions.

We have arrived at the Legion of Skanks, guys.” Walking the midways, they caught Luis J. Gomez for a brief, on-the-move hello; he thanked them, in their telling, and moved on. “We’ve got a slight interaction with Burt and that probably counts.” A fan also stopped to say hello to Burt. Kick captions, which were messy for the Gomez exchange, so it is paraphrased.

Then the mechanical bull: “Excuse me, can my friend have a free bull ride possibly?” “Excellent. Free.” Burt rode first, and a fan asked for a photo with him. Ted rode in the orange Flyers jersey, a free curb-alert find in his telling. “Damn, Ted, you’re doing great.” “Good job, Teddy.” Kick captions and stills.

stories.headline: HeelMike Fought OBS in a Rhinestone Skull Mask, Then Asked the Big Question: “Do You Think TwitchCon Will Let Me In?”
stories.deck: The Slots & Casino chapter of his birthday: 1 hour, 6 minutes, 13 seconds, about 45 minutes of setup, and an on-screen wallet that ended below where it started.
stories.body: HeelMike’s 32nd birthday would not end. At 5:29 a.m. ET he was back live from the stay in a silver rhinestone skull mask and a purple-and-gold baroque shirt, ready to gamble, except for OBS. A Google search, “HOW TO ADD CHROME TAB TO OBS,” made the broadcast. Then he issued a clarification to the nation: “What I meant was, do you think TwitchCon will let me in with this mask?” Told the setup took 45 minutes, he answered: “All I need is three minutes.” The on-screen wallet slid from $839.78 to $118.52. Closing statement: “I want to end stream.”
stories.pull_quote: Do you think I’m a fucking rookie? I’m not losing my money in five minutes. All I need is three minutes.

record.date_label: Saturday, Nov. 14, 5:29:09 a.m. ET to about 6:35:22 a.m. ET (1 hour, 6 minutes, 13 seconds)
record.label: The Slots & Casino continuation of HeelMike’s birthday night, a separate tape from the already-reported birthday VODs 137744695, 137763434 and 137767984 and the short reconnect 137772934; it went live about 18 seconds after that reconnect ended. Official Kick duration 3,973,000 ms (1 hour, 6 minutes, 13 seconds). Category Slots & Casino; English; marked mature. Livestream / VOD 137773276. Kick’s public API showed 17,738 VOD views at the 7:07 a.m. ET refresh and 103,539 followers. Concurrent viewers this desk saw live (Kick public API): 4,172 at about 5:59 a.m. ET and 4,217 at 6:05:40 a.m. ET. These are sampled checks, not an official peak. Cold approaches: 0; this was an indoor stay and an on-screen blackjack session. Private people on the broadcast are not named.

Back live at the stay in a black T-shirt and silver chain, camera low: “We have to we have to go live again.” Then: “Things lagging. I feel like when I touch stuff it lags.” Scar was with him. He could not figure out how to change his stream title. Whisper pass on the official VOD audio.

Noticing that “PUBG mobile is still a category,” he proposed that the punishment for a “terrorist crime against America” should be “live streaming 30 hours a day, PUBG Mobile,” closing on a fake payout screen: “Congratulations your KPP paid out $3.08.” Whisper pass.

He said he was “dehydrated as shit,” that they “stole my water,” and later: “Habibi, I’m a baby. Just give me a goddamn water.” He apologized, “it’s my birthday,” and asked, “how do I gamble.” Whisper pass.

The second look of the night: a silver rhinestone skull mask and a purple-and-gold baroque short-sleeve shirt. “Are you guys ready to gamble. The funniest mask ever. I need to see what this mask looks like with the Mario hat.” Then: “All we need now is the Mario hat and I can’t lose.” The Mario cap from the earlier tapes is not on his head in the stills; he was looking for it. Whisper pass and stills.

An OBS card appeared on screen: “You’ve just added a browser source.” He asked, “Why is it raining in San Diego?” and ruled out the balcony because “the internet might not reach out there.” First he asked whether “Discord will let me in wearing this hat,” then corrected himself: “What I meant was, do you think TwitchCon will let me in with this mask? … Holy dude my brain cells are actually deteriorating and I said that so seriously.” Whisper pass and stills.

A still at 40:00 shows a Google search on screen, “HOW TO ADD CHROME TAB TO OBS.” They window-captured the casino, locked the camera, and he repeated a placement rule: “Stake specifically said the camera can go anywhere except for blocking the Stake logo.” Stills and whisper pass.

Someone in the room: “It took you 45 minutes to set up the casino. You’re gonna lose it all in five minutes.” HeelMike: “Sounds like a challenge. Do you think I’m a fucking rookie? I’m not losing my money in five minutes. All I need is three minutes.” Kick captions and whisper pass.

The Stake.us blackjack wallet, as displayed on screen in the desk’s minute stills (not a verified cash-out or settled balance): $839.78 at 44:00, a peak of $1,999.78 at 52:00, $494.78 at 57:00 and $994.78 at 60:00, when he said: “Okay chat, we’re right back where we started.” The laptop was “fighting from one percent,” and “we don’t have a real charger.” Stills and whisper pass.

The last still, at 65:00, shows the on-screen wallet at $118.52, the mask off and HeelMike grimacing over an Ace-4 against a dealer 9. “I just want blackjack. Yes, I love having a 12 and busting. It’s my favorite thing in the world.” At 1:06:02: “I want to end stream.” The VOD ends about 11 seconds later. Whisper pass, lightly cleaned, and stills.

stories.headline: HeelMike Wore a Mario Cap, Admitted Chloe Yummy Was “Literally Taller Than Me,” and Got Home Declaring: “I Am Not Chub.”
stories.deck: The next 1 hour, 7 minutes, 40 seconds of his San Diego birthday: a sidewalk height ruling, an Uber Premium SUV and a pose he wants in bodybuilding.
stories.body: HeelMike’s 32nd birthday entered its next chapter in a white Mario cap. On the sidewalk, someone told him, “don’t lie to yourself you’re short as hell.” He conceded on the record: “Chloe Yummy was literally taller than me.” He said he “felt like Wartortle.” In the back of what he called an Uber Premium SUV, he nominated his own move for the sport: “the call is such a sick pose that I actually think it should be a bodybuilding pose one day.” Back at the stay, he issued a denial: “I am not chub.”
stories.pull_quote: Chloe Yummy was literally taller than me.

record.date_label: Saturday, Nov. 14, 4:17:02 a.m. ET to about 5:24:42 a.m. ET (1 hour, 7 minutes, 40 seconds), plus a reconnect from 5:24:51 a.m. ET (4 minutes, 12 seconds)
record.label: The next chapter of HeelMike’s San Diego birthday night, a separate tape from the already-reported birthday VODs 137744695 and 137763434: a club, downtown sidewalks, an Uber and the group’s stay. Official Kick duration 4,060,000 ms (1 hour, 7 minutes, 40 seconds). IRL; English; not marked mature. Livestream / VOD 137767984. Kick’s public API showed 14,476 VOD views on the desk’s first pull at about 5:59 a.m. ET and 14,478 at the 6:05:40 a.m. ET refresh. The reconnect coda (VOD 137772934, 252,000 ms) showed 15,326 views. 103,536 followers at the 6:05:40 a.m. ET refresh. Concurrent viewers this desk saw live (Kick public API): 2,042 at about 4:55 a.m. ET and 2,411 at 5:02 a.m. ET. These are sampled checks, not an official peak. Cold approaches: 0 scored; this was a party tape, not a cold-approach stream. Private people on the broadcast are not named.

The tape opened in a dark, purple-lit club, HeelMike in a white cap with a red Mario “M,” a black T-shirt and a silver chain. The white cap from the earlier continuation is, on this tape, clearly a Mario hat. He told chat he “was just farming content and then everyone thought I was crazy, which I’m not.” The stream lagged almost immediately: “I’m offline for the night I just lag again.” Kick captions and stills.

“Oh my fucking back dude I’m thirty two years old.” He told chat, “we will be right back,” and a 10:00 still shows him outside the club in the same Mario cap and black shirt. Kick captions and stills.

Outside at night, he said he was “kind of tall, very big.” Someone told him, “don’t lie to yourself you’re short as hell.” He announced, “it’s my thirty second birthday.” A man in the conversation, not named here, invited the group line dancing. HeelMike: “Can we go line dancing?” No number handoff was confirmed, and FNN is not scoring it as an approach. Kick captions.

To Scar: “Panda was screaming, get in the Uber, get in the Uber, get in the Uber, and I was saying it to you eight times. But you’re the only reason we’re live right now… W Scar, we are using our phone.” Kick captions, checked against the desk’s recap clip.

Realizing “we’re all going to the same Airbnb,” he admitted he “was a little insecure because she was… low key taller than me,” said he “felt like Wartortle,” and ruled: “Chloe Yummy was literally taller than me.” Kick captions.

In the Uber, he recapped the night for chat: “We’ve been there for four and a half hours we’re not done yet and we ended stream and then we’ve been live for thirty minutes.” Shoutouts followed, including “yo everyone say yo what up Tarzan.” Kick captions.

He said he almost “donated a penny to myself,” then coached a back-seat pose: “the call is such a sick pose that I actually think it should be a bodybuilding pose one day.” He repeated that he is 32. Kick captions.

He said he was in an “Uber… Premium SUV,” called the driver “hardworking,” and said he “always tip[s] and get[s] five stars,” talking about bumping the tip because a light was in the driver’s face. On the first stop: “was not my house what am I doing doesn’t even remotely look like it.” Those are his words. Kick captions.

Arriving at the stay: “I’m back. Where am I? Okay. Yeah. Hey guys. All right. We’re live. Why would this be put here? Who made this, Scarlet? I am not chub.” English auto-captions stop at 46:34; FNN reports the rest of the official VOD from stills only and quotes no dialogue after that point. Kick captions, checked against audio.

On the 4-minute-12-second reconnect from inside the stay, Scar sometimes held the camera. HeelMike: “I’ll probably wake up around like nine in the morning. Make sure you charge it.” Then: “W’s in the chat for Scar.” He was back live by 5:29 a.m. ET on a new stream, which FNN will cover when that VOD posts. Kick captions.

stories.headline: Skankfest Said No Streaming, So Burt Bronx and Ted Streamed a Hotel Room for 4 Hours, 38 Minutes. Ted Fit in a Suitcase.
stories.deck: After-hours Day 1 in New Orleans: a fan on speaker, a $10,000 kickflip bounty, a kiss Ted refused, and a plan to “work around” the rule.
stories.body: Skankfest X told Burt Bronx and Ted they couldn’t stream inside the tents, because comedians fear “joke poaching.” At 12:13 a.m. ET they went live from a New Orleans hotel room and stayed there 4 hours, 38 minutes. A fan called in on speaker. A $10,000 text-to-speech bounty dared Ted to teach Burt a rolling kickflip within a month. A noise in the hall sent Ted into a suitcase, and he fit: “We could have saved so much on travel.” Chat demanded a kiss; Ted offered “kissing through my hand.” Sign-off: Salvo lands tomorrow, and “we’ll finally work around it.”
stories.pull_quote: We’ll try to stream earlier now that we understand the protocol at Skankfest. We’ll finally work around it.

record.date_label: Saturday, Nov. 14, 12:13 a.m. ET to about 4:51 a.m. ET (4 hours, 38 minutes, 6 seconds)
record.label: Late hotel-room stream after Day 1 of Skankfest X in New Orleans, with his travel partner Ted on camera the whole time. A second “BURT BRONX AT SKANKFEST DAY 1” tape, separate from the 7:13–8:23 p.m. ET Friday stream (VOD 137702995). Official Kick duration 16,686,000 ms (4 hours, 38 minutes, 6 seconds). Why no festival footage: “they have a policy that says that we’re not allowed to stream at Skankfest because apparently some of the comedians” worry about “joke poaching,” so streamers stay out of the tents, “where they do, like, their exclusive material.” Their read: “If you get labeled as a joke stealer in the comedy world, it’s almost… it’s not a complete death sentence, but… people will yell at you.” Fans recognized Burt from Fish Tank: “That was really cool.” Kick captions.

Then a $10,000 text-to-speech challenge landed: if Ted can teach Burt to land a kickflip on stream within a month, rolling, the money is his. “He cannot do it standing still.” Ted’s assessment: “the best we could hope for would be a non-moving one on carpet.” Not attempted on this tape. Kick captions.

stories.headline: HeelMike Turned 32 at TwitchCon. Panda Went to Wendy’s, and Scar Took the Stream: “That’s a Little Too Good.”
stories.deck: HeelMike’s 3-hour-21-minute San Diego birthday tape went street, 7-Eleven, a muted mod, a bar and a club, with Scar holding the camera.
stories.body: HeelMike turned 32 at midnight in San Diego and made it a state occasion. He opened with “I’m so old,” titled the stream after an Ice Poseidon event he says he skipped, “for SEO purposes,” and renewed his annual grievance: “I show up to TwitchCon every year and they never let me in.” Panda promised a club table, then, by HeelMike’s account, went to Wendy’s. He accidentally muted his longtime mod, Tarzan, then got him back. He handed the camera to Scar, who told chat, “I’m cosplaying Mike.” He says she gained him 600 views: “That’s a little too good.”
stories.pull_quote: I show up to TwitchCon every year and they never let me in.

record.date_label: Friday, Nov. 13, 11:41 p.m. ET, to about 3:03 a.m. ET Saturday, Nov. 14 (3 hours, 21 minutes, 10 seconds), plus a continuation from 3:14 a.m. to about 4:02 a.m. ET (47 minutes, 57 seconds)
record.label: IRL birthday night from San Diego during TwitchCon: a downtown street, a 7-Eleven, cars, a bar, an SUV and a club. Official Kick duration 12,070,000 ms (3 hours, 21 minutes, 10 seconds). IRL; tags Adventure; English; not marked mature. Livestream / VOD 137744695. Kick’s public API showed 20,904 VOD views at about 3:55 a.m. ET; the continuation (VOD 137763434, 2,877,000 ms) showed 17,599 views at the 4:05 a.m. ET refresh. 103,534 followers at that refresh, up from 103,517 at the first live flag around 12:05 a.m. ET. Concurrent viewers this desk saw live (Kick public API): about 1,251 at 12:05 a.m. ET, 4,830 at 2:03 a.m. ET and 4,325 at 3:01 a.m. ET; 4,180 on the continuation at about 3:55 a.m. ET. These are sampled checks, not an official peak. Cold approaches: 0 scored; this was a party tape, not a cold-approach stream. Private people on the broadcast are not named.

He came up already talking: “I’m so old thirty two and thirty minutes.” He set the title on the tape: “HeelMike’s birthday I am at TwitchCon I am not at Ice [Poseidon] Safe Zone event but that is in my title for SEO purposes.” The raw caption reads “Ice Beside”; Ice Poseidon is rendered from context and from the API title. He said it is “my birthday at midnight.” FNN is not confirming his whereabouts beyond what the tape and API show. Kick captions.

At the turn: “chat we are alive and it’s my birthday guys it’s my birthday.” Edwin gifted 10 subs. He claimed they are “the number one gifted sub on the whole entire website,” which was not verified. Panda arrived with “my name is Panda I’m more famous than him.” He called Chloe Yummy “a mega star superstar” and repeated, “I show up to TwitchCon every year and they never let me in.” Kick captions.

At a 7-Eleven he tried on heavy black sunglasses, the “abusive dad sunglasses” look he had asked for, and gave chat a birthday fit check: a black Travis Matthew tee he says cost “seventy dollars,” Nordstrom pants with a “custom waist of twenty eight inches,” and size-11 shoes. Frames confirm the store interior and the sunglasses rack. Kick captions.

Split from the group, he said he had “called Panda no exaggeration thirty one times.” In his recap, Panda announced “we got a table” and then went to Wendy’s, leaving two people from the group waiting in a club lobby. In the next car he realized he had “permanently muted” his longtime mod Tarzan, asked how to unmute, and got Tarzan back, among what he called “the three people muted ever in my kick career.” This is his account of Panda’s night, not independently checked. Kick captions.

At a bar he called “W Scar” as Scar took shots with him, ripped a contact lens and swapped in a spare. He said Scar is “actually like a really good streamer” and that he gained six hundred views while she was on: “I wanted you to do good but like that’s a little too good.” He also said he has “one point two million on Twitch” and left for Kick “because Kick paid me more,” his own figures, not an API check, and called multi-streaming “the stupidest thing ever” because it “annihilates your negotiating power.” Kick captions.

In a departing SUV with Panda, in a Chicago Bulls hoodie and a TwitchCon badge, and Scar, in a gold chain (visually confirmed in a 2:56 still), he laid out the night: “we’re going all night tonight… we’re gonna gamble tonight we’re gonna do a giveaway tonight.” Then: “Scar is gonna hold down the stream for about thirty minutes chat… I’ll be back in thirty minutes.” He went back to the group’s stay; the reason he gave is not reported here. Kick captions.

Scar held the camera outside the club: “I know that you think I’m Mike… but I’m Scarlet… he’s ten minutes away,” and, “I’m streaming on Mike’s [stream] I’m cosplaying Mike he’s not here right now.” Someone told her “Panda has a section.” Around 0:10 HeelMike rejoined, thanked her for “holding it down for a minute,” and by about 0:14 the group was inside a dark, packed club, him in a white sailor-style cap and sunglasses. Captions largely stop at 0:16 in the club noise, so FNN is not reporting dialogue after that point. The tape ended around 4:02 a.m. ET. Kick captions and stills.

stories.headline: A Masked Driver Called “License,” a Drift That Never Happened, 0 for 6. Clavicular’s Verdict: “Gypsy Cursed Me.”
stories.deck: 3 hours, 49 minutes from shotgun on a Miami-area highway to the sidewalk: a 17-minute BRB, “hunter eyes,” a bar he called “giga aids” and the Standard.
stories.body: Clavicular went live at 9:01 p.m. ET Friday riding shotgun beside a balaclava-wearing Duel.com driver chat calls License. “He could drive, bro.” The promised drift never happened. After a 17-minute BRB card, he worked a restaurant patio: “Can’t give you a baby, but I can give you a good night.” He activated his “hunter eyes,” called Miami “a cope” and left a packed bar calling it “giga aids.” A sit-down with a Duel-affiliated guest he called “Gypsy” produced “Chad has no race.” By FNN’s count of the tape, six cold approaches landed zero numbers. His verdict: “Gypsy cursed me.”
stories.pull_quote: Can’t give you a baby, but I can give you a good night.

stories.headline: Flights Grounded, Burt Bronx Made Skankfest Anyway. Then: Two Sets of 12 Squats and a ChatGPT Itinerary.
stories.deck: Day 1 of Skankfest X in New Orleans, Ted on camera: a Blood Pit pitch, boardwalk squats in a borrowed jacket, no MAGA hat and a panel that had just ended.
stories.body: “All the flights were grounded,” Burt Bronx told chat Friday, “and I still was able to fly out today somehow.” He went live at 7:13 p.m. ET from Day 1 of Skankfest X in New Orleans, Ted on camera. At the Blood Pit ring he volunteered: “I’ll do it for content. Until I get my ass kicked.” Chat ordered squats; he did two sets of 12 on the boardwalk in Ted’s too-small jacket. A MAGA-hat scavenger hunt found no hat. The panel he wanted had just ended, so he asked ChatGPT for an itinerary. Next stop: the Florida Man Tent.
stories.pull_quote: I mean, I’ll do it for content. Until I get my ass kicked, I’ll do it for content.

record.date_label: Friday, Nov. 13, 7:13 p.m. ET to about 8:23 p.m. ET (1 hour, 10 minutes, 1 second)
record.label: IRL stream from Day 1 of Skankfest X, the Legion of Skanks comedy festival at Mardi Gras World in New Orleans (Nov. 13–15), with his usual co-host Ted on camera. Official Kick duration 4,201,000 ms (1 hour, 10 minutes, 1 second). IRL; tags Adventure; English; marked mature. Livestream / VOD 137702995. 520 VOD views at the 8:58 p.m. ET check. 9,344 followers at that check. Concurrent viewers this desk saw live (Kick API): 117 at 8:03 p.m. ET, the only mid-stream check. record.label: On the first live shot, a two-shot with Ted: “Made it, chat. All the flights were grounded, and I still was able to fly out today somehow.” Speech-to-text on the stream audio.
record.source: Kick VOD, Burt Bronx, “BURT BRONX AT SKANKFEST DAY 1”

record.label: At the outdoor Blood Pit ring under “SKANKFEST X BLOOD PIT” screens, during the evening Skankfights window, Ted said, “Burt is definitely going to enter the fight, guys.” Burt answered chat: “I mean, I’ll do it for content. Until I get my ass kicked, I’ll do it for content.” A clown-costumed wrestler then scored a knockdown. Burt did not enter the ring on this tape.
record.source: Kick VOD, Burt Bronx, “BURT BRONX AT SKANKFEST DAY 1”

record.label: Cold, he asked Ted, “Do you mind if I wear your jacket, I’m just a little cold,” and put on Ted’s dark ES zip-up skate jacket, which Ted said would be “super small” on him. Chat called him “so cute in Ted’s jacket” and ordered squats; he did two sets of 12 on the wooden boardwalk, which they called a cooldown: “those two sets of twelve reps.” It was the night’s only training session.
record.source: Kick VOD, Burt Bronx, “BURT BRONX AT SKANKFEST DAY 1”

record.label: A scavenger-hunt text-to-speech message asked them to find a MAGA hat; none turned up on this tape. Burt’s read on the festival: “I have no idea what Skank Fest was. Honestly we kind of showed up and we’re still learning. It kind of looks like a mixed event of like just like carnival rides and outdoor sets.” He said VIP access had sold out before he could get it.
record.source: Kick VOD, Burt Bronx, “BURT BRONX AT SKANKFEST DAY 1”

record.label: In the red-curtained Cabaret Cave tent, they were told the event they came for, “Would You Bang Him,” had “just now” ended, around 6:47–6:53 p.m. CT. The official Friday schedule listed it from 6:00–7:30 p.m. CT; this desk reports both and offers no explanation. Ted then read a ChatGPT prompt for the “highest ROI” remaining events “as of now, 7 p.m. CST.” In their telling, it pointed them to the Florida Man Tent.
record.source: Kick VOD, Burt Bronx, “BURT BRONX AT SKANKFEST DAY 1”

record.label: At the Florida Man Tent, Burt asked for a Michelob Ultra. Around 0:54:04 they said, “Mark Normand’s on stage right now.” They found seats for the 7 p.m. CT showcase and watched a comic’s stand-up set. When staff asked them to clear filming with the bosses, Ted’s introduction was “Burt Bronx from season three of Fish Tank,” and a staffer called them “the nicest.” The stream closed on its Fish Tank bumper.
record.source: Kick VOD, Burt Bronx, “BURT BRONX AT SKANKFEST DAY 1”

stories.headline: Shut Out of the Partner Party, He Says, HeelMike Paid a Segway Stranger $50. By Dawn: “We All Work Together Forever.”
stories.deck: HeelMike’s 3-hour-40-minute San Diego TwitchCon opener went bar, street, a lost Stake hand, a $50 handoff, a stranger’s car and Panda’s Raising Cane’s.
stories.body: HeelMike went live at 2:57 a.m. ET in downtown San Diego, announced “I am a morning streamer now,” and spent three hours and 40 minutes building a TwitchCon empire. He says he missed a flight, got turned away from the partner party and won three grand off camera, figures he later contradicted. On camera, he lost a Stake blackjack hand, handed a photographer he’d just met $50 instead, ordered onion-loaded hot dogs he named “the Chernobyl,” and rode in the stranger’s car to the rental, where Panda was eating Raising Cane’s. His verdict: “Now we all work together forever.”
stories.pull_quote: I am coming to TwitchCon to start no problems. Have fun. So bring good vibes.

record.label: IRL stream from San Diego for TwitchCon: downtown bars and streets, a street hot-dog cart, a ride in a photographer’s car, the crew’s rental, and a 24/7 grocery store. Official Kick duration 13,205,000 ms (3 hours, 40 minutes, 5 seconds). IRL; tags Adventure; English; marked mature. Livestream / VOD 137569223. 20,948 VOD views at the 7:02 a.m. ET check. 103,517 followers at that check, up from 103,487 at the first live flag around 3:02 a.m. ET. We missed one flight.” Kick captions. No giveaway drawing happens on this tape.
