record.label: His account of the TwitchCon partner party: “I went to the partner party … and they didn’t let me in, which is bullshit. … They thought I was some other dude.” Speech-to-text and captions agree; this is his version of what staff said, not a confirmed official notice. He also said, “I gambled off camera today. I won three grand, so I’m in a good mood.” Later in the stream he said he “lost a thousand dollars gambling on Stake” and that he had “gambled three grand.” His figures do not reconcile and were not verified.
record.source: Kick VOD, HeelMike, “HEELMIKE vs TWITCHCON PT 1”

record.label: He met a photographer on the street and advised him to shoot streamers outside the convention when it closes: “Trust me, you’ll blow up. … I’m actually giving him sauce, chat.” After losing a short Stake blackjack hand while trying to send him money, he said, “I’ll give you 50 because I lost my money. Fifty dollars.” Kick captions.
record.source: Kick VOD, HeelMike, “HEELMIKE vs TWITCHCON PT 1”

record.label: At a street cart he ordered hot dogs with “extra onions,” later “four orders of onions,” and named them “the Chernobyl.” The bill in captions was $33.99. He recapped the travel day: “I missed my flight, lost five hundred dollars, booked another flight.” The $500 is his figure. Kick captions.
record.source: Kick VOD, HeelMike, “HEELMIKE vs TWITCHCON PT 1”

record.label: The photographer drove the crew to the rental, where the streamer Panda, in a grey tie-dye hoodie, was eating Raising Cane’s at the table (visually confirmed). HeelMike asked chat for an over/under on fights he would have to break up and said, “I am coming to TwitchCon to start no problems. Have fun. So bring good vibes.” In the car he told the photographer, “A $250 ticket. I’m gonna buy it for you. … You could be the driver.” The ticket purchase was not seen on this VOD. Kick captions.
record.source: Kick VOD, HeelMike, “HEELMIKE vs TWITCHCON PT 1”

record.label: On the ride back, wearing a metallic skull mask and a black fur vest, he recapped the night: the crew gave a stranger $50, got in his car, went to a grocery store, and “now we all work together forever.” His close: “We’ll be live long Friday, long Saturday, long Sunday. … I love you guys. Good night.” Kick captions, lightly cleaned for roll.
record.source: Kick VOD, HeelMike, “HEELMIKE vs TWITCHCON PT 1”

stories.headline: He Swore Off Hard Liquor and Cooked Butter Chicken “to Perfection.” Then Came King Street and “Like Two Shots.”
stories.deck: CobbRuvs’ nine-hour Toronto marathon went condo kitchen, freezing sightseeing walk, then Stake, ending on a $12 parlay he says pays $2,300.
stories.body: CobbRuvs spent nine hours and 14 minutes turning a Toronto condo he says runs about $110 Canadian a night into a culinary landmark. He billed himself as “the first white American to ever cook the main Canadian cuisine out here,” announced mid-sear that he’d quit hard liquor, and fought a touchscreen stove to the verdict: “This is some of the best butter chicken I’ve ever had, and it’s cooked to perfection.” Then came a freezing King Street walk, where he admitted to “like two shots,” and a Stake session ending on a $12 parlay he says pays $2,300.
stories.pull_quote: This is some of the best butter chicken I’ve ever had, and it’s cooked to perfection.

IRL on the finished VOD object; mature; English. Highest concurrent viewer counts this desk saw live (Kick API): 1,168 / 1,165 around 1:05 a.m. ET Friday and 1,061 at 8:02 p.m. ET Thursday; these are sampled checks, not an official peak. record.label: “We’re cooking butter chicken and rice, the first white American to ever cook the main Canadian cuisine out here. We’re cooking butter chicken! Who’s ever cooked butter chicken in the chat? This might taste like straight shit. I haven’t really looked it up.” Speech-to-text confirmed.
record.source: Kick VOD, CobbRuvs, “BEERS & COOKING STREAM [BUDDER CHICKEN]”

record.label: “This hotel was like a hundred and ten Canadian a night. It’s not a hotel. I’m damn near in an apartment condo out here. The CN Tower is right behind this building right here.” Speech-to-text confirmed. He said it was booked through Expedia; the price is as he stated it.
record.source: Kick VOD, CobbRuvs, “BEERS & COOKING STREAM [BUDDER CHICKEN]”

record.label: While the chicken thighs seared: “I quit drinking hard liquor. … I can’t really get drunk off Cutwaters or Coronas … Does anyone proud of me? Like, that takes a lot as a man.” Speech-to-text confirmed. He also fought the touchscreen cooktop, which kept flashing error codes and shutting off, and called it something that should be “banned.”
record.source: Kick VOD, CobbRuvs, “BEERS & COOKING STREAM [BUDDER CHICKEN]”

record.label: “The butter chicken is done. Try it. … Kill me right now if I’m lying. This is some of the best butter chicken I’ve ever had, and it’s cooked to perfection.” Speech-to-text confirmed and checked against a 90-second clip of the tasting. He served the woman in the apartment first; her on-tape review was mixed (“pumpkin-y,” “really sweet,” then “it’s pretty good”). He said next time he would add more cream and cut the pieces smaller.
record.source: Kick VOD, CobbRuvs, “BEERS & COOKING STREAM [BUDDER CHICKEN]”

record.label: Outside: “Welcome to Canada. We’re all miserable and cold.” At a bar he talked himself into “one shot can’t hurt, right, boys.” Walking home on the King Street IRL, he said he “went back on [his] word” with “like two shots” and “let [himself] down.” Several bars and clubs would not let him film openly. (Caption-based.)
record.source: Kick VOD, CobbRuvs, “BEERS & COOKING STREAM [BUDDER CHICKEN]”

record.label: Back in the apartment he played Stake slots, blackjack and keno called by chat. He built an NBA parlay he described as $12 to win $2,300: “What’s $12 hitting for? $2,300 off the $12. … Boom. Bet placed.” Speech-to-text confirmed. The payout figure is his on-stream claim; this desk did not settle the slip, and the result was unknown at filing. Sign-off over leftover butter chicken: “And that’s how we’re sending it off for now. On a nice quiet meal, chug a drink, and send you on your way.”
record.source: Kick VOD, CobbRuvs, “BEERS & COOKING STREAM [BUDDER CHICKEN]”

stories.headline: He Turned 38 at Exactly 2:38 a.m., Live on Kick. Then He Stayed On Six More Hours.
stories.deck: Burt Bronx’s nine-hour birthday stream hit the official minute on a Discord call, then rolled through a nap, a blood-test booking and his New Orleans plans.
stories.body: Burt Bronx says he was born at 2:38 a.m. EST, so his 38th birthday stream ran past midnight to catch the minute. On a Discord call with Fish Tank’s Jimmy, he announced: “It is 2:38 a.m. EST. I'm now officially 38 years old.” Then he kept going: a nap through the new Love and Justice episode, a morning blood-test booking. Skankfest with Ted is still on for Friday: “I bought the tickets, the plane trip's already booked, the hotel's booked. That's happening. So deal with it.” He’s staying in Jersey, not moving to LA. Sign-off: “This was fun.”
stories.pull_quote: It is 2:38 a.m. EST. I'm now officially 38 years old.

record.label: “Just give me like twenty minutes to rest.” He played the new Love and Justice episode and was asleep on the couch in the 5:00:00 VOD frame while it played. Earlier he said: “We just filmed the first two episodes of the second season [of Love and Justice]. We should film the other two episodes somewhere late November.” (Caption-based.)

I feel like since everything [going on with] my sister and my family, it's probably best I stay in Jersey for at least [a bit].” (Exact closing clause unclear on tape.)

stories.headline: He Said He’d Gotten It to Eight Grand Off Camera. Then He Lost $6,500 in 15 Minutes.
stories.deck: HeelMike said he’d gotten to eight grand off camera, then lost $6,500 in 15 minutes. On-stream, the overlay peaked at $1,702.38 and was last sampled at $81.39.
stories.body: Thursday after 1:45 a.m. ET, HeelMike ran an 18-minute-56-second Stake.us blackjack stream. He said he’d been gambling off camera, “got it all the way to eight grand,” then “lost 6.5 thousand dollars in 15 minutes.” His claims, not a verified withdrawal. The first overlay sample showed $1,597.38. “This is destined for failure. I had it all. I had it all. I had it all. I ruined it,” he said. stories.headline: He Said He’d Be Back in 30 Minutes. An Hour and a Half Later, He Showed a Reinstalled Expander.
stories.deck: Wednesday night, Hexumlite returned later than promised and showed a reinstalled expander from the passenger seat. The first one, he said, had started to bend.
stories.body:
Wednesday night, Hexumlite came back after the off-stream FME appointment, later than the 30 minutes he had promised, a 21-minute-4-second VOD from the passenger seat, an unnamed woman driving toward Sprouts.

It was a reinstall. He said the prior FME had started to bend, and a healing palatal split was cut back through with a saw. FaceGenics, he said, covered the replacement as an appliance error. He showed the new expander on camera.

Kick captions heard 38.9 millimeters. He was “in too much pain” for cold approaches, and signed off to get “twist comboed,” and “maybe Growler, too.”
stories.pull_quote: “The FME device itself had some structural integrity issues. And so starting to bend, in order to expand safely we had to take it out…”

And so starting to bend, in order to expand safely we had to take it out… It was pretty easy. You just had to let it heal up a little bit where the screws were and then we just reinstalled because we want to get more expansion.” Then: “So spare apparently my split was starting to heal up. stories.headline: Sunday, Jeffries Was a “Hard Yes.” Tuesday, the House Referred It 211-204.
stories.deck: Massie was the only Republican who voted to keep the Hegseth impeachment alive. Jeffries: “This is not the end of it.”
stories.body:
Sunday, on ABC’s This Week, House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries was asked if Democrats would back Rep. Thomas Massie’s impeachment of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. “I’m a hard Yes on the Hegseth resolution,” he said. “Pete Hegseth has got to go.”

Tuesday at 6:02 p.m., the House voted 211-204 to refer H. Res. 1655 to the Judiciary Committee. Republicans voted 210-1. Massie was the only Republican with the 203 Democrats who voted no. One independent voted yes.

That morning, Hegseth called it a “farce.” After the vote, Jeffries said: “This is not the end of it. It’s just the beginning.”
stories.pull_quote: I’m a hard Yes on the Hegseth resolution. … Pete Hegseth has got to go.

record.label: Roll Call 317, 6:02 p.m.: On Motion to Refer H. Res. 1655 (impeaching Peter Brian Hegseth), Passed, 211-204, 18 not voting. Republicans 210-1-0-7; Democrats 0-203-0-11; Independent 1-0-0-0
record.source: Office of the Clerk, U.S. House

record.label: Jeffries on ABC’s This Week: “I’m a hard Yes on the Hegseth resolution. … Pete Hegseth has got to go.” Also: “I believe there will be incredibly strong support for that resolution.”

House voted 211-204 to refer the resolution to Judiciary, “effectively killing it”; Massie the lone Republican against referral; Massie: “I wasn’t surprised, but I was disappointed”; Jeffries after the vote: “This is not the end of it. It’s just the beginning.” Hegseth, at a morning news conference: “farce” and “political spectacle”; “None of these are high crimes or misdemeanors.” Trump, CBS reported, said it “miserably FAILED!”
Hegseth: “It’s a farce, and it’s a stunt and everybody knows it.” Jeffries has said Democrats will “run Pete Hegseth out of town” when they take over next year, NBC reported

stories.headline: Musk: The Order Rate “Far Exceeds” Production. He’ll “Return Deposits for a Lot of People.”
stories.deck: The Cybertruck line shuts down in about eight months, he said, for Cybercab. “Not a case of Cybertruck being unprofitable, as has been misreported.”
stories.body:
Friday, Elon Musk said Tesla would wind down Cybertruck production at Gigafactory Texas “around the middle of next year to make room for increased Cybercab production.”

Monday: “The Cybertruck order rate far exceeds our production rate. We will try to make as many as possible before shutting down the line in about 8 months, but will have to return deposits for a lot of people.”

He added that this “is not a case of Cybertruck being unprofitable, as has been misreported by legacy media,” but a matter of “opportunity cost.” He did not name the outlets.
stories.pull_quote: This is not a case of Cybertruck being unprofitable, as has been misreported by legacy media.

record.label: Musk: “The Cybertruck order rate far exceeds our production rate. We will try to make as many as possible before shutting down the line in about 8 months, but will have to return deposits for a lot of people.” Full text continues: “This is not a case of Cybertruck being unprofitable, as has been misreported by legacy media, but rather that the opportunity cost of the complexity of Cybertruck is vastly outweighed by the value of incremental Cybercab production.”
Musk: “Tesla will be winding down production of the Cybertruck at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year to make room for increased Cybercab production”
Musk, replying: “We are still building Cybertruck for another 8 or 9 months btw, but then Tesla needs to focus on scaling Cybercab. There will never be another vehicle like it.”
Musk: the order backlog is “far more than we can make before dismantling the line for Cybercab expansion around June/July next year. We will add an extra shift to try to get all orders done in time.”

Washington voters just kept the state’s tax on income over $1 million, 58% to 42%. Same ballot, same voters: Initiative 638 passed with 56%, more than 1.6 million yes votes in the latest count.

stories.body:
Nov. 2, at a live Pivot taping, Hillary Clinton took up President Trump’s talk of pardoning Elon Musk. A pardon, she said, “does not remove the obligation to respond to a subpoena in the Congress.” “Some legal experts argue,” she added, that if you’re pardoned, “You cannot take the Fifth Amendment because you have no jeopardy.” Then: “So let him pardon Elon, and then let’s call him in and figure out what he has to say.”

In July, after a Biden pardon, Anthony Fauci took the Fifth more than 100 times. The hedge was “experts.” The ask was hers.

stories.deck: A federal appeals panel said the Pittsburgh-area parish is “very likely to prevail.” On Monday, the full court declined to rehear its bid to build now.

Holy Trinity Ukrainian Catholic Church outside Pittsburgh wants a shrine that would “honor Mary, the Mother of God, and would pay homage to the sanctity of life.” Collier Township refused to rezone, citing traffic and fundraising. After the hearing, a commissioner emailed: “Looks like we might have dodged a bullet last night.”

In October, a Third Circuit panel found the parish “very likely to prevail” but denied an injunction: “Preliminary injunctions exist to preserve cases, not decide them.”

stories.headline: “Gratitude Is the Fruit That Makes Everything Else Taste Sweet”: Charlie Kirk’s Last Thanksgiving Message
stories.deck: Kirk called Thanksgiving a “uniquely American tradition” and said thanks belong “To the Almighty God.” Erika Kirk showed what that looks like in grief.
stories.body:
In his 2024 Thanksgiving message, Charlie Kirk called the holiday a “uniquely American tradition,” Fox News reported. “I think it speaks very well to our nation that there is a day when we stop and say thank you.”

His point: “Gratitude is the fruit that makes everything else taste sweet. But then you must be thankful to whom? To the Almighty God.”

On Thanksgiving 2025, her first without him, Erika Kirk wrote: “It’s easy to fixate on what’s been taken, at what’s missing. But my goodness does the Lord meet me in my weakness.”

And: “What remains is sacred.”

stories.headline: From 6% to 19%: Evangelicals Are Now the Largest Faith Group in Honduras, Guatemala and El Salvador
stories.deck: A 30-year Latinobarómetro survey of 17 countries also finds evangelicals more likely than Catholics to say they practice their faith.
stories.body:
Latinobarómetro’s 2025/2026 religion report finds evangelicals are now the largest religious group in Honduras (44%), Guatemala (43%) and El Salvador (42%). Those are pluralities, not majorities, Infobae notes.

Region-wide, evangelicals are 19% of Latin Americans, up from 6% in 1995, per Evangelical Focus. Catholics fell from 80% to 55%.

Evangelicals take it seriously: 62% call themselves practicing, against 48% of Catholics.

Researchers describe a “profound transformation of the religious landscape in Latin America over the last three decades,” in The Christian Post’s translation. They also found more young people among the nonreligious.

stories.headline: “Ring the Church Bell Three Times”: As Christmas Nears, West Bengal’s Christians Prepare Under the Shadow of Attacks
stories.deck: A Christian forum in the Indian state counts dozens of incidents since May. Its plan: a bell alarm that brings neighbors of every faith running.
stories.body:
West Bengal’s Christian forum, the Bangiya Christiya Pariseba, told churches Tuesday: if “any suspicious or unfamiliar group enters the church or pastorate compound, anyone present should immediately ring the church bell three times,” The Telegraph reported. Neighbors “irrespective of faith” are to gather and “stand peacefully in solidarity beside the pastor.”

Its rule: “Do not engage in physical altercations.”

The forum counts 48 to 65 incidents since May, International Christian Concern reports. At one church inauguration, a member told The Hindu: “Some miscreants entered while we were praying.” Police called it, prima facie, a feud between two Christian groups.

stories.headline: “My Message Has Never Been About Promoting Intolerance”: Felix Nmecha, 26, Lays His Crown Down

stories.headline: “Steps Are Not Results”: A Year After Nigeria’s U.S. Designation, Officials Tell Congress “the Violence Has Not Stopped”
stories.deck: At a House hearing Nov. 12, State Department officials credited Nigeria with some steps. Rep. Riley Moore: “we cannot take this CPC designation off.”
stories.body:
A year after the U.S. designated Nigeria a “country of particular concern” for religious freedom, a House Foreign Affairs subcommittee asked on Nov. 12 what has changed.

“Unfortunately, the violence has not stopped,” Assistant Secretary of State Frank Garcia said, Reuters reported. Assistant Secretary Riley Barnes called the violence against Christians “appalling.”

Nigeria has hired police and increased arrests, Barnes said, but Christians in the Middle Belt are not safer for it.

Rep. Riley Moore, R-W.Va.: “But steps are not results.” And: “we cannot take this CPC designation off this country.”

Nigeria’s government rejected the designation as based on misinformation.

On Wednesday, Nov. 11, students from different churches gathered in Red Square, the brick plaza at the heart of the University of Washington campus in Seattle, for an afternoon of worship. They worshiped “for hours,” CBN News reported.

Pastor Jesse Bradley, a former pro soccer player and chaplain for the Seattle Sounders, shared the gospel and handed out Bibles.

stories.headline: They Sold Their Couch to Adopt From Liberia. Nine Years Later, the Hepworths Went Back to See Where It Began.
stories.deck: Young missionaries with little money said yes to two children in Liberia. A church couple gave a car. This National Adoption Month, they are a family of six.
stories.body:
Zac and Ebie Hepworth were young missionaries with very little money. So they sold their couch to help pay for an adoption, then ate pizza on the floor of their empty living room, Lifesong for Orphans recounts.

A couple from church donated a car. A Lifesong matching grant became “a bridge of courage,” Ebie said.

In June 2017 they flew one-way to Liberia and became a family of four. Their son was later diagnosed with a serious genetic condition. Zac weighed it: “No comparison.”

Twins followed. Now they have gone back to Liberia together.

stories.headline: “Chaplains Should Not Be Forced to Give Up Their Religious Beliefs”: A Fired Hospice Chaplain Goes to the EEOC
stories.deck: The Rev. Richard Blue moved his family to Michigan for the job. Days in, he says, HR asked about a personal Facebook post. Weeks later, he was out.
stories.body:
The Rev. Richard Blue, an ordained Lutheran minister and board-certified chaplain, moved his family to Michigan for a full-time job with Heartland Hospice.

About two days in, First Liberty Institute says, his supervisor and HR asked about a “religious post” on his personal Facebook page. Blue says HR asked how he could care for LGBTQ patients. His answer: his beliefs “do not prevent me from giving compassionate, respectful, and equal care.”

He says he was fired July 9. First Liberty filed an EEOC charge. Heartland did not immediately respond to the Free Press.

This is a charge, not a ruling.

“Saying you’re a Christian and living your life in obedience to Christ is not necessarily the same thing,” she told students, the Liberty Champion reported.

A junior: “Wearing the costume of holy is not the same as living holy.”

She closed: “Here I am, Lord. Send me.”

On Oct. 30, bulldozers in Peshawar, Pakistan, tore down at least 13 Christian homes and a Pentecostal church, UCA News reported. Most of the families are poor sanitation workers.

The reason, per an official notice: a plan to “beautify Peshawar and transform it into a city of flowers.” Authorities claim the homes sat on government land. No compensation.

Rashida Stephen says her family got three days’ notice. “We barely manage one meal a day. We are government workers and deserve justice.”

The Church of England baptized 9,900 adults in 2025, up by a third, figures released Friday show. The church’s report calls adult baptisms “quite possibly higher than they have ever been,” the Church Times reported.

stories.deck: His last book, finished a month before he was killed, makes the case for the Sabbath. Erika says it made him a “next-level husband.”
stories.body:
At 28, Charlie Kirk told a pastor he was hitting a wall and “drinking eight cups of coffee a day just to stay afloat.” The pastor asked: “Are you honoring the Sabbath?”

Kirk pushed back: “I will honor God by working harder, not by resting for a day.” Then he changed his mind, and wrote his last book about it, finished one month before he was killed.

“If the Sabbath can change my life, it can change everyone’s life,” he wrote.

Erika Kirk says he became “a next-level husband.” Her advice: “Pour into them. That’s your legacy.”

stories.headline: “Even If You Cut Me Into Pieces”: A 20-Year-Old Coptic Deacon Is Killed in Libya After Refusing to Deny Jesus

Milad Malak, 20, was a deacon at a Coptic church in Egypt’s Gharbia governorate who went to Libya for work, Open Doors reported. On Oct. 4, Islamic State militants kidnapped him and two Muslim friends in Zliten, International Christian Concern reported.

stories.headline: Fired for Their Faith, Vindicated in Court: Appeals Court Leaves $7.8 Million BART Verdict Standing
stories.deck: Six Bay Area transit workers lost their jobs after seeking religious exemptions from a 2021 vaccine mandate. The Ninth Circuit won’t take another look.
stories.body:
In 2021, 181 Bay Area Rapid Transit employees asked for religious exemptions from BART’s COVID-19 vaccine mandate. According to the appellate opinion, BART accommodated none of the 70 it deemed eligible, and 73 lost their jobs.

Six sued. In October 2024, a federal jury found BART never showed that accommodating them would be an undue hardship, and awarded $7,824,580.

A Ninth Circuit panel unanimously affirmed in September. Now the court has denied BART’s rehearing request, Pacific Justice Institute announced Nov. 11.

Faith goes to work, too.

stories.deck: Pew figures show 41% of Americans ages 18 to 22 attend services at least monthly, more than adults overall. A few birthdays later, it drops to 27%.
stories.body:
America’s youngest adults are showing up. A Pew Research Center analysis reported by the Deseret News found 41% of 18- to 22-year-olds attend religious services at least monthly, versus 33% of all adults. Young men, at 47%, outpace young women, at 35%.

The warning: at ages 23 to 26, it falls to 27%. Pew’s Chip Rotolo calls it “mixed signals.”

Barna found prayer is the top spiritual reason young adults give for going. “They’re showing up for the simple offerings,” says Barna’s Daniel Copeland.

Researchers want more data before calling it a resurgence. It is an open door.

stories.headline: “That Is Discrimination Against Religion”: Federal Judge Opens Tennessee’s Charter Program to a Christian School
stories.deck: A federal judge ruled Tennessee’s ban on religious charter schools violates the First Amendment, clearing Wilberforce Academy of Knoxville to apply.
stories.body:
Since 2002, Tennessee law required every public charter school to be “nonsectarian” and “nonreligious.” On Friday, Nov. 6, U.S. District Judge Charles Atchley ruled for Wilberforce Academy of Knoxville, a proposed tuition-free Christian charter school. “The First Amendment does not permit Tennessee to open its charter school program to private participants and then exclude them because they seek to exercise their religion,” he wrote, quoting Carson v. Makin. “That is discrimination against religion.”

The ruling covers Wilberforce and Knox County. The district is reviewing it; any appeal would go to the Sixth Circuit.

stories.headline: Courage for His Faith: A First Reflection on the Life and Love of Charlie Kirk
stories.deck: He asked to be remembered for courage for his faith. His widow, Erika, and a growing campus movement still carry the work.
stories.body:
June 29, 2025: Charlie Kirk said he wanted to be remembered “for courage for my faith.” “The most important thing is my faith.”

He co-founded Turning Point USA in 2012 and married Erika in 2021. They had two children. On Sept. 10, 2025, he was assassinated at Utah Valley University, at 31.

Eleven days later, Erika told his memorial, “I forgive him because it was what Christ did, and it is what Charlie would do.” On Oct. 14, his 32nd birthday, President Trump awarded him the Medal of Freedom. A year later, CNN reported 1,500 college chapters, up 64 percent.

Trump posthumously awarded Kirk the Presidential Medal of Freedom in the White House Rose Garden on what would have been Kirk’s 32nd birthday; Erika accepted. The president also proclaimed that date a National Day of Remembrance for Charlie Kirk.

stories.headline: CORRECTION: The Boston Globe Regrets the Article
stories.deck: The Globe said voters think Massachusetts is “a worse place to live.” Then it reported they’ll reelect the management.
stories.body:
Oct. 20, the Boston Globe: “Many voters believe Massachusetts has become a worse place to live, a Suffolk University/Boston Globe poll found. They want to reelect Governor Maura Healey anyway.”

The numbers: 42% say worse. 15% say better. 55% say taxes are too high. Healey leads Republican Mike Minogue, 59% to 36%.

Massachusetts has a Democratic governor and Democratic supermajorities in both chambers: 35 of 40 Senate seats, 131 House seats.

One party owns the results. The Globe called it “a worse place.” FNN fixed one word: the worst.

stories.headline: Obama Lectures on Omar’s ‘Nonexistent Smoking Gun.’ Brennan’s Notes Say He Was Briefed on the Clinton Plan.
stories.deck: NBC and CNN quoted the sermon. They skipped the notes.
stories.body:
Oct. 18: Barack Obama posted a sermon. The government “can’t selectively target individuals” for their politics. The Omar probe, he wrote, hunts “a nonexistent smoking gun.”

NBC and CNN quoted the sermon. Neither mentioned the notes.

In 2016, CIA Director John Brennan briefed Obama on intelligence alleging Hillary Clinton approved a plan to “vilify” Trump with a Russia scandal. U.S. intelligence says it can’t vouch for that claim. The FBI never checked: Durham found it “never opened any type of inquiry,” while running a full investigation of Trump associates on raw, uncorroborated information.

Selective targeting. He would know.

stories.headline: Ed Markey Wants to Abolish the Fire Department While His State Hands Out Matches
stories.deck: Markey calls ICE “thugs” over street arrests. His own state’s rules are why ICE makes street arrests.
stories.body:
Sen. Ed Markey, Oct. 19: “Trump’s ICE thugs.” In September he called ICE “a domestic terror organization.”

Here’s why agents are on the street. In 2017, Massachusetts’ highest court ruled local officials can’t hold anyone solely on an ICE detainer. Boston’s Trust Act limits cooperation with federal immigration authorities. In January, Gov. Healey barred ICE from using state property as a staging area.

In May 2025, ICE said many of its 1,461 Massachusetts arrests came after local jurisdictions “refused to honor immigration detainer requests.”

Lock the jailhouse door. Then complain about the sidewalk.

stories.headline: JPMorgan Said It Never Debanks for Politics. Here’s What the Federal Regulator Found.
stories.deck: A bank’s CEO can say anything at a shareholder meeting. A watch list is harder to argue with.
stories.body:
May 21, 2019, JPMorgan’s shareholder meeting. Jamie Dimon: “We have not and do not debank people because of their political views.”

Oct. 14, 2026: the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency found that from 2020 to September 2025, all nine of the largest banks had such policies.

JPMorgan’s payment company flagged “MAGA, Make America Great, and America First.” An employee scrubbed “right wing” and “religious” from a nonprofit’s file.

To be fair: one bank turned away a group whose political arm endorsed only Democrats. The weight of the examples is not close.

stories.headline: Letitia James Unveils Justice System That Cuts Out the Middleman: the Facts and the Law
stories.deck: New York’s top law enforcement officer, on camera: “You don’t have to look at the facts and the law.”
stories.body:
Oct. 8, the New York attorney general debate on Spectrum News NY1. The topic was prediction markets. Republican Saritha Komatireddy, a former federal prosecutor, said she has to look at the facts and the law.

Attorney General Letitia James corrected her: “You don’t have to look at the facts and the law. All you have to do is study what they do. It is illegal in the state of New York, period.”

Asked to name a past attorney general she admires, James paused. She later named Bob Abrams.

The job is looking at the facts and the law.

stories.headline: The Boston Globe Finally Unmasked the Man Behind Mass Daily News
stories.deck: He is a software engineer. He has a laptop. Readers follow him. The Globe ran a profile.
stories.body:
Oct. 10: the Boston Globe combed through public records and named the man behind Mass Daily News. Simon Pacheco, 36, a Boston software engineer. He runs the site alone, nights and weekends.

The Globe’s case: the site is largely AI-written, and its posts attack Mayor Michelle Wu.

The Globe’s own admission: the site “has broken some news, including the arrest of a City Hall employee that the Globe subsequently reported on.”

One man and a phone beat the Globe to a City Hall arrest. The Globe responded by finding out his name.
